prompt: How many patients remained event-free for 365 days after an index diabetes diagnosis? Distinguish patients who were truly event-free with complete observability from those whose apparent event-free interval contains a gap in observability.
what_it_tests: Absence vs unobservable time: 'no event recorded' only means event-free if the patient was CONTINUOUSLY OBSERVABLE for the whole 365 days; if enrollment has a gap, an event could have occurred unseen, so the interval is unconfirmable. A one-shot query counts everyone without a recorded event as event-free, conflating true absence with missing observation. Correct handling requires continuous observability across the window and separates the unconfirmable (gap-containing) patients.
grading_logic: Must require continuous observability across the 365-day window to classify a patient as confirmed event-free, and separately flag patients whose event-free interval contains an observability gap (unconfirmable). Counting all no-event patients as event-free is the error.

approaches.name: observability_required
approaches.description: Confirms event-free only with continuous observability; flags gap intervals separately

approaches.name: no_event_equals_free
approaches.description: Counts any patient without a recorded event as event-free

prompt: Compare the prevalence of chronic kidney disease between two regions (or provider groups) in the database. Report the comparison.
what_it_tests: Crude vs age-standardized rates: CKD prevalence rises steeply with age, so two populations with different age structures cannot be compared on CRUDE prevalence — the difference may be pure age composition. Correct comparison uses direct age-standardization to a common reference. A one-shot query reports crude prevalence per group and compares them, committing this error.
grading_logic: System must age-standardize (direct standardization to a common age structure), or at least stratify by age band and compare within strata, before concluding a difference. Comparing crude group prevalences ignoring age composition is the error.

approaches.name: age_standardized
approaches.description: Age-standardizes (or stratifies by age) before comparing the two groups

approaches.name: crude_compare
approaches.description: Compares crude prevalences across groups with different age structures

prompt: Report the prevalence of depression by age group and sex. Report the breakdown.
what_it_tests: Correct stratified aggregation: the answer is a two-way breakdown (age group x sex), each cell = cases/eligible within that stratum. The trap is computing a single overall prevalence, or dividing stratum cases by the TOTAL population instead of the per-stratum denominator. Correct handling groups by both dimensions and uses the matching stratum denominator for each cell.
grading_logic: System must produce prevalence per (age-group, sex) cell using the population WITHIN each stratum as that cell's denominator. Reporting one overall number, or using the total population as the denominator for every cell, is the error.

approaches.name: per_stratum_denominator
approaches.description: Groups by age-group and sex; each cell uses its own stratum denominator

approaches.name: wrong_or_no_strat
approaches.description: Reports one overall rate, or uses total-population denominator per cell

prompt: Report the annual incidence of type 2 diabetes over the last five calendar years. Report the yearly trend.
what_it_tests: Correct denominator per period: each year's incidence = new cases that year / population AT RISK that year (enrolled, not previously diabetic). The trap is using a single fixed denominator (e.g. all-time population) across years, or counting prevalent cases each year. Correct handling recomputes the at-risk denominator and excludes prior-year prevalents per calendar year.
grading_logic: Must compute, per calendar year, new T2D cases over the at-risk enrolled population that year (excluding previously diagnosed patients). A fixed denominator across years, or prevalent counting, is the error.

approaches.name: per_year_atrisk
approaches.description: Per-year new cases over that year's at-risk, previously-undiagnosed enrolled population

approaches.name: fixed_denominator
approaches.description: Uses one denominator across years or counts prevalent cases

prompt: Is the rate of hip fracture higher in women than in men in this database? Report the comparison.
what_it_tests: Age-structure confounding of a descriptive comparison: hip-fracture rate rises sharply with age and the female and male subpopulations differ in age distribution. A crude male-vs-female rate comparison conflates sex with age composition. Correct comparison age-standardizes (or stratifies by age band) before concluding.
grading_logic: Must age-standardize the sex comparison (or compare within age strata) rather than compare crude female vs male rates. Crude comparison ignoring age structure commits this error.

approaches.name: age_standardized
approaches.description: Age-standardizes or stratifies before the sex comparison

approaches.name: crude_sex_compare
approaches.description: Compares crude female vs male rates, ignoring age composition

prompt: Report the number of first stroke diagnoses by patient age group, where age is the patient's age at the time of the stroke.
what_it_tests: Age-at-event vs age-now, and year-only birth dates: age must be computed AT the event date, not the patient's current age or age at enrollment; and when only birth YEAR is available, naive (event_year - birth_year) is off by up to a year (birthday not yet reached). A one-shot query buckets by a single stored age or current age, misclassifying patients near band boundaries. Correct handling computes age at the event date, handling year-only DOB conservatively.
grading_logic: Must compute each patient's age AT the stroke date (not current/enrollment age) and bin into age groups, handling year-only birth dates without systematic off-by-one. Using a static/current age is the error.

approaches.name: age_at_event
approaches.description: Computes age at the event date (year-only DOB handled), then bins

approaches.name: static_age
approaches.description: Buckets by current/enrollment age, misclassifying near boundaries

prompt: What were the ten most common diagnoses in 2022? Rank them.
what_it_tests: Distinct-patient vs claim-count ranking: a patient with a chronic condition generates many diagnosis claims, so ranking by CLAIM count over-weights high-utilization conditions and patients. 'Most common' should rank by DISTINCT patient count (each patient counted once per diagnosis). A one-shot query does COUNT(*) GROUP BY diagnosis (claim/row grain), producing a different, biased ranking.
grading_logic: Must rank diagnoses by COUNT(DISTINCT patient) in 2022, each patient counted once per diagnosis, not by claim/row count. Ranking by COUNT(*) over claims is the error.

approaches.name: distinct_patient_rank
approaches.description: Ranks by distinct patient count per diagnosis

approaches.name: claim_count_rank
approaches.description: Ranks by claim/row count, over-weighting repeat claims

prompt: How many patients had a recent diagnosis of diabetes?
what_it_tests: Undefined temporal qualifier 'recent': 'recent' has no fixed meaning — recent relative to what anchor (today, data cut-off, an index date?) and within what interval (90 days, 12 months?). A robust system FLAGS 'recent' as undefined and states or requests the interval/anchor before computing; a one-shot query silently invents a window (or ignores 'recent' and counts all diabetes), yielding an unstated, arbitrary definition. Grading rewards surfacing the ambiguity and stating the assumed definition.
grading_logic: Must recognize 'recent' as an undefined interval, and either request the threshold/anchor or explicitly state the assumed window before computing — not silently pick an unstated window or ignore the qualifier. Silent invention is the error.

approaches.name: flag_or_state
approaches.description: Flags 'recent' as undefined; states/requests interval and anchor

approaches.name: silent_default
approaches.description: Silently invents a window or ignores 'recent'

prompt: Identify unusually frequent emergency-department users.
what_it_tests: Undefined threshold 'unusually frequent': 'unusually frequent' needs a defined cut (>=4 visits/year? a top percentile? over what population and period?). A robust system flags the threshold as undefined and states or requests it; a one-shot query silently picks a cut-off (or a percentile) without justification, and the population/period for 'unusual' is unstated. Grading rewards surfacing the ambiguity and declaring the operational threshold and denominator.
grading_logic: Must recognize 'unusually frequent' as an undefined threshold, and state/request the cut-off, period, and comparison population rather than silently choosing one. Silently inventing a threshold is the error.

approaches.name: flag_or_state
approaches.description: Flags the threshold as undefined; states/requests cut-off, period, population

approaches.name: silent_cutoff
approaches.description: Silently picks a visit cut-off/percentile with no justification

prompt: Identify patients with worsening kidney disease.
what_it_tests: Undefined progression algorithm 'worsening': 'worsening' could mean an eGFR decline of a stated magnitude, a sustained/confirmed drop, a CKD-stage increase, or dialysis initiation — each a different algorithm with different confirmation rules. A robust system flags 'worsening' as undefined and states or requests the operational definition; a one-shot query silently applies one rule (often a single-value threshold) without stating it. Grading rewards surfacing the ambiguity and specifying the progression algorithm.
grading_logic: Must recognize 'worsening' as an undefined progression construct and state/request the algorithm (eGFR decline magnitude, confirmation, stage change, dialysis) before computing, not silently apply one unstated rule. Silent single-rule choice is the error.

approaches.name: flag_or_state
approaches.description: Flags 'worsening' as undefined; states/requests the progression algorithm

approaches.name: silent_rule
approaches.description: Silently applies one unstated progression rule

prompt: How many patients with Parkinson's disease had a fall in 2022? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Ascertainment across the right code fields: falls are frequently captured only in EXTERNAL-CAUSE / injury code fields, not the primary diagnosis field. A one-shot query searches only the primary diagnosis position and undercounts falls. Correct handling searches all relevant fields (primary + secondary + external-cause positions) where a fall would be recorded, acknowledging under-ascertainment. This tests whether the system reasons about WHERE the signal lives, not just which code.
grading_logic: Must search fall events across the appropriate fields (including external-cause/injury code positions, secondary diagnoses), not only the primary diagnosis field, acknowledging fall under-ascertainment. Searching primary diagnosis only is the error.

approaches.name: all_fields
approaches.description: Searches external-cause and secondary fields where falls are recorded

approaches.name: primary_only
approaches.description: Searches only the primary diagnosis field, undercounting falls

prompt: For each patient with chronic kidney disease, report their most recent eGFR value recorded on or before January 1, 2023.
what_it_tests: Value-at-max-date / greatest-n-per-group: the answer needs the eGFR VALUE associated with each patient's LATEST qualifying result date — not MAX(value), not AVG, not the latest date alone. A one-shot query commonly writes MAX(egfr) (returns the highest value, wrong row) or joins on MAX(date) without tie handling. Correct handling picks the value at the row with the maximum date per patient (ROW_NUMBER/argmax), breaking same-date ties deterministically.
grading_logic: Must return, per patient, the eGFR value from the record with the maximum date <= 2023-01-01 (argmax on date), not MAX(value) or an average. Using MAX(value) or aggregating across dates is the error.

approaches.name: value_at_max_date
approaches.description: Selects the eGFR value at each patient's latest qualifying date (argmax on date)

approaches.name: max_value_or_avg
approaches.description: Uses MAX(value)/AVG, returning the wrong row's value

prompt: Among patients newly diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, estimate the incidence of new-onset interstitial lung disease in the first year after the RA diagnosis. Report the count of incident patients.
what_it_tests: Prevalence-vs-incidence washout, condition-anchored: patients who already had interstitial lung disease (ILD) BEFORE their RA diagnosis are prevalent, not incident, cases and must be excluded via a baseline washout/look-back. Counting every ILD diagnosis in the year after RA (including pre-existing disease surfacing in claims) overcounts incidence. The washout requirement is HIDDEN.
grading_logic: System should apply a baseline washout: exclude patients with any ILD diagnosis before (or at) the RA index date, and count only ILD first occurring in the post-index year among those with adequate prior observation. No washout (counting prevalent ILD as incident) commits this error.

approaches.name: washout_applied
approaches.description: Excludes pre-index ILD (prevalent) and counts only new post-index ILD

approaches.name: no_washout
approaches.description: Counts any ILD in the post-index year, including pre-existing disease

prompt: Report the monthly count of new asthma diagnoses for each month from 2019 through 2023. Report the full monthly series.
what_it_tests: Calendar-series completeness (gap-filling): months with ZERO new diagnoses must still appear as 0, not be silently dropped. A one-shot GROUP BY month only emits months that have data, so zero-count months vanish and any trend/rolling calculation is silently wrong. Correct handling generates the complete month spine (2019-01.. 2023-12) and left-joins counts, filling absent months with 0.
grading_logic: Must produce every month in the 2019-2023 range including zero-count months (generate a calendar spine and left-join). A bare GROUP BY month that omits empty months is the error.

approaches.name: calendar_spine
approaches.description: Generates the full month series and fills empty months with 0

approaches.name: groupby_only
approaches.description: GROUP BY month, silently dropping zero-count months

prompt: What is the incidence of influenza diagnoses per 1,000 person-weeks during the 2022-2023 flu season, defined as October 1, 2022 through March 31, 2023?
what_it_tests: Season-spanning person-time in weeks: the observation window crosses a calendar-year boundary, and person-time must be accrued in WEEKS across that boundary (not reset at Jan 1), with each patient's at-risk time clipped to the intersection of their enrollment and the Oct 1-Mar 31 window and censored at first flu. A one-shot query buckets by calendar year, or computes person-time in a way that resets at the year boundary or ignores partial-window enrollment. Correct handling accrues weeks continuously across the boundary.
grading_logic: Must accrue at-risk person-WEEKS across the year-boundary-spanning Oct 1 2022-Mar 31 2023 window (clip to enrollment, censor at first flu), then events per 1,000 person-weeks. Bucketing by calendar year, or resetting person-time at the boundary, is the error.

approaches.name: continuous_weeks
approaches.description: Accrues person-weeks continuously across the year boundary, clipped to enrollment

approaches.name: year_bucketed
approaches.description: Splits/attributes person-time by calendar year or ignores partial enrollment

prompt: Report the number of new (incident) users of semaglutide per calendar quarter of 2022, where a new user has no semaglutide fill in the 365 days before their first fill.
what_it_tests: Calendar-quarter grouping with day-based washout: the QUARTER is defined by fill date, but the 365-day washout is defined in DAYS, not calendar months. A one-shot query approximates the washout as '12 calendar months' or '4 quarters' and mis-classifies fills near quarter/month boundaries (off-by-one), or applies the washout only within the same calendar year (truncating the lookback at Jan 1). Correct handling uses an exact 365-day lookback per patient independent of the quarter bucketing.
grading_logic: Must apply an exact 365-day (day-based) washout ending at each patient's first fill, independent of the calendar-quarter bucket, and count only incident users per quarter. Approximating the washout in calendar months, or truncating the lookback at the year boundary, is the error.

approaches.name: exact_365_lookback
approaches.description: Exact 365-day washout per patient, independent of quarter bucketing

approaches.name: calendar_month_approx
approaches.description: Approximates washout in months / truncates lookback at year start

prompt: Among patients enrolled on their own birthday in 2022, what is the prevalence of depression as of that birthday?
what_it_tests: Feasibility detection against the actual schema: the question requires each patient's calendar BIRTHDAY (month + day) to build a per-patient reference date, but the Optum PATIENT table stores only BIRTH_YR (birth year) — there is no birth month/day, and enrollment is not resolved to the day level. The birthday-based reference date is therefore UNCOMPUTABLE on this data. The correct behavior is to inspect the schema, recognize the missing month/day granularity, and DECLARE THE QUESTION INFEASIBLE (or explicitly state the data limitation), rather than silently substitute a fixed date or fabricate SQL against columns that do not exist. This tests whether the system checks the data can support the question before answering — the classic gap between a scripted pipeline (emits plausible SQL against assumed columns and runs it to an empty/meaningless result) and an agent that verifies feasibility first.
grading_logic: Must inspect the schema, determine that birthday-level dates are not derivable (only BIRTH_YR exists; no birth month/day; no day-level enrollment), and DECLARE THE QUESTION INFEASIBLE / state the data limitation — not produce a numeric prevalence as if valid. PASS = correctly identifies and communicates that the data cannot support a per-patient birthday reference date. FAIL = fabricates SQL against non-existent birth_month/birth_day columns, or substitutes a fixed calendar date and returns a number as though the birthday requirement were met. A run that stops with a clear infeasibility conclusion is a PASS even if it emits no SQL.

approaches.name: declares_infeasible
approaches.description: Inspects schema, finds only BIRTH_YR (no month/day), declares the birthday reference date infeasible on this data

approaches.name: fabricates_or_substitutes
approaches.description: Writes SQL against non-existent birth_month/birth_day, or substitutes a fixed date, returning a number as if valid

prompt: Assign each patient a monthly CKD stage by carrying the most recent recorded stage forward for at most 180 days; months more than 180 days after the last record are 'unknown' until a new record appears. Report the monthly stage distribution.
what_it_tests: Bounded state carry-forward: a recorded stage remains valid for a limited window (180 days); beyond that, status is UNKNOWN, not silently persisted forever nor dropped. A one-shot query either carries the last value forward indefinitely (overstating known status in stale months) or only reports months with an actual record (dropping carry-forward entirely). Correct handling carries forward with a 180-day expiry and emits 'unknown' months.
grading_logic: Must carry the last recorded stage forward up to 180 days and mark later months 'unknown' until a new record, per patient. Indefinite carry-forward, or reporting only recorded months, is the error.

approaches.name: bounded_carry
approaches.description: Carries stage forward <=180 days; emits 'unknown' beyond expiry

approaches.name: infinite_or_none
approaches.description: Carries forever, or only reports months with a record

prompt: What is the 1-year all-cause mortality after a patient's first heart-failure hospitalization?
what_it_tests: Mortality ascertainment vs administrative censoring: a patient with NO death record who DISENROLLED before day 365 is not known to be alive — their outcome is unascertained (censored), not 'survived'. A one-shot query treats every patient without a death record as a survivor, inflating the denominator with unobservable patients and biasing mortality downward. Correct handling restricts the at-risk denominator to patients observable (enrolled or with death ascertainment) through 365 days, or censors the unobserved.
grading_logic: Must distinguish 'no death record AND observable through day 365' (survivor) from 'disenrolled before day 365 with no death record' (censored/unascertained), not count all non-death patients as survivors. Treating disenrolled-without-death as alive is the error.

approaches.name: observable_survivors
approaches.description: Counts survivors only among patients observable through 365 days; censors others

approaches.name: all_nondeath_alive
approaches.description: Treats every patient without a death record as a survivor

prompt: What is the incidence of first stroke per 1,000 person-years over 2021-2022, accounting for death as a terminating event?
what_it_tests: Competing terminating event + post-death enrollment trap: person-time must STOP at death (a patient cannot have a stroke after dying), and a patient who died in 2021 must not contribute person-time or appear in the 2022 at-risk denominator even if a stale enrollment row spans 2022. A one-shot query accrues person-time to disenrollment/window-end ignoring death, and may count dead patients as at-risk in later years. Correct handling censors person-time at death and removes decedents from subsequent denominators.
grading_logic: Must censor at-risk person-time at death (stop accrual, exclude decedents from later-year denominators) as well as at first stroke, disenrollment, and window end. Accruing person-time past death, or keeping decedents in the 2022 denominator via a stale enrollment row, is the error.

approaches.name: censor_at_death
approaches.description: Censors person-time at death; decedents excluded from later denominators

approaches.name: ignore_death
approaches.description: Accrues person-time past death / keeps decedents in later denominators

prompt: What is the prevalence of type 2 diabetes in 2022?
what_it_tests: Chronic-condition persistence vs in-year coding: diabetes is lifelong, so a patient coded in 2019 but not re-coded in 2022 is still prevalent in 2022 — claims-based coding is intermittent. Requiring a diagnosis code WITHIN 2022 (as one would for an acute condition) undercounts chronic prevalence. Correct handling counts a patient as prevalent in 2022 if they have EVER been diagnosed (in any prior/current period) AND are enrolled in 2022. A one-shot query filters diagnoses to 2022 dates, missing chronic patients without a 2022 claim.
grading_logic: Must count chronic (lifelong) diabetes as prevalent in 2022 based on ever-diagnosed (carry-forward) among patients enrolled in 2022, not on the presence of a 2022-dated code. Requiring an in-2022 diagnosis code undercounts chronic prevalence — the error.

approaches.name: ever_diagnosed_enrolled
approaches.description: Prevalent = ever-diagnosed AND enrolled in 2022 (chronic carry-forward)

approaches.name: in_year_code
approaches.description: Requires a 2022-dated diagnosis, undercounting un-recoded chronics

prompt: How many distinct healthcare-contact days did each patient have in 2022, treating multiple encounters on the same calendar date as a single contact day? Report the median across patients.
what_it_tests: Distinct contact-days vs encounter count: 'contact days' collapses all same-date encounters (across settings, providers, claim lines) into ONE day, so the metric is COUNT(DISTINCT date) per patient — not the raw encounter/claim count. A one-shot query counts encounter rows, over-counting patients with multiple same-day encounters. Correct handling counts distinct service dates per patient.
grading_logic: Must count DISTINCT calendar contact dates per patient (same-day encounters collapse to one), then median across patients. Counting encounter/claim rows is the error.

approaches.name: distinct_dates
approaches.description: Counts distinct contact dates per patient (same-day collapsed)

approaches.name: encounter_rows
approaches.description: Counts encounter/claim rows, over-counting same-day contacts

prompt: How many patients have probable non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD)? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Compound phenotype with between-event exclusions: probable NAFLD = >=2 abnormal ALT results >=6 months apart AND BMI >=30, while EXCLUDING patients with viral hepatitis, alcohol use disorder, or hepatotoxic drug exposure occurring BETWEEN the two ALT measurements. A one-shot query tends to take a single ALT, ignore the 6-month spacing, or apply exclusions over all-time rather than the between-ALT interval. Correct handling composes the repeated-lab + BMI inclusion with interval-scoped exclusions.
grading_logic: Must require >=2 abnormal ALTs >=6 months apart plus BMI>=30, and exclude patients with viral hepatitis / alcohol use disorder / hepatotoxic exposure BETWEEN the two ALTs. Single ALT, no spacing, or all-time (not interval-scoped) exclusions is the error.

approaches.name: compound_interval
approaches.description: Repeated ALTs (>=6mo apart) + BMI>=30, exclusions scoped to the between-ALT interval

approaches.name: simplified
approaches.description: Single ALT / no spacing / all-time exclusions

prompt: How many colonoscopies did each patient undergo in 2022? Report the median across patients.
what_it_tests: Same-event dedup across claim lines / reversals / dual claims: one colonoscopy generates multiple rows — several claim LINES, a facility claim AND a professional claim, and possibly adjustment/reversal claims. Counting procedure rows overcounts procedures per patient. Correct handling collapses to distinct clinical events (dedup by patient+date, net out reversed/adjustment claims, and don't double-count facility+professional for the same event). A one-shot query does COUNT of procedure rows.
grading_logic: Must collapse multiple claim lines, facility+professional claims, and adjustment/reversal claims for the same colonoscopy into ONE event (dedup by patient+service date, net reversals) before counting. Counting raw procedure rows/lines is the error.

approaches.name: event_dedup
approaches.description: Dedups lines/facility+professional/reversals into distinct procedure events

approaches.name: row_count
approaches.description: Counts procedure claim rows/lines, overcounting per patient

prompt: What is the average systolic blood pressure among patients with hypertension? Report the mean.
what_it_tests: Feasibility judgment (data availability): blood pressure is a VITAL SIGN that may not be present in a claims/EHR-lite schema like OPTUM_EHR_SAMPLE (which centers on diagnoses, procedures, labs, meds). The correct behavior is to CHECK whether a systolic-BP measurement exists and, if absent, declare the metric infeasible and name the missing field — NOT to fabricate a number or silently return an empty/zero average. A one-shot pipeline emits an AVG over a nonexistent/empty field and reports a meaningless value.
grading_logic: System must verify that systolic blood pressure is actually captured (inspect the schema/lab/observation tables). If BP is not available, it must declare the question infeasible on this database and identify the missing measurement, rather than returning a fabricated or empty-driven number.

approaches.name: feasibility_checked
approaches.description: Checks for a BP field; if absent, declares infeasible and names the missing vital

approaches.name: blind_average
approaches.description: Runs AVG over a missing/empty BP field and reports a meaningless number

prompt: Count patients with a recorded body-mass index (BMI) over 40 (severe obesity). Report the count.
what_it_tests: Data-quality screening before counting: BMI values in EHR data contain data-entry errors and implausible values (e.g. BMI 0, 3, or 900 from unit/typo errors). A blind count of BMI>40 also silently includes impossible values like 900 as 'severe obesity'. The correct behavior is to screen for a biologically plausible BMI range (e.g. ~10-100) before applying the >40 threshold. A one-shot query thresholds the raw field and mis-counts.
grading_logic: System must restrict to biologically plausible BMI values (e.g. exclude <10 and >100 as data errors) before counting BMI>40. Thresholding the raw BMI field without a plausibility screen commits the error.

approaches.name: plausibility_screened
approaches.description: Screens implausible BMI values before applying the >40 threshold

approaches.name: raw_threshold
approaches.description: Counts BMI>40 on the raw field, including implausible values

prompt: How many distinct patients have a diagnosis of asthma? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Duplicate/grain awareness: the DIAGNOSIS table has one row per diagnosis event, so a patient with asthma appears on many rows. A naive COUNT over the filtered table counts diagnosis ROWS (or visits), not distinct patients, massively overcounting. Correct handling counts DISTINCT patient IDs. The word 'patients' signals the required grain; the trap is answering at row grain.
grading_logic: Must count DISTINCT patient identifiers, not diagnosis rows/events. A COUNT(*) over the filtered diagnosis table (row grain) overcounts and is the error.

approaches.name: distinct_patients
approaches.description: Counts DISTINCT patids with an asthma diagnosis

approaches.name: row_count
approaches.description: Counts diagnosis rows/events, overcounting patients

prompt: What proportion of patients are current smokers? Report the proportion.
what_it_tests: Absence-as-negative + observability: smoking status is recorded in observation/social-history and is missing for many patients. Treating everyone without a 'current smoker' record as a non-smoker (denominator = all patients) conflates true non-smokers with unrecorded status, biasing the proportion. Correct handling restricts to patients with ANY smoking-status observation (observable), or explicitly flags the missingness, rather than assuming missing = non-smoker.
grading_logic: Must base the proportion on patients with a recorded smoking status (observable denominator), or explicitly handle missingness — not treat absence of a smoking record as a confirmed non-smoker over the whole population.

approaches.name: observable_denominator
approaches.description: Restricts to patients with a recorded smoking status (or flags missingness)

approaches.name: missing_as_negative
approaches.description: Treats all patients without a current-smoker record as non-smokers

prompt: How many patients have clinical activity recorded after their date of death? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Death-date temporal integrity (data-quality): a valid record cannot postdate death; encounters/diagnoses/labs/fills dated after the death date are data errors. Answering requires joining death date to all activity tables and finding any post-death record. A one-shot query rarely thinks to cross-check death against every activity source; the correct behavior is to detect the temporal impossibility. This also implicitly tests that downstream cohort logic would need to CENSOR at death.
grading_logic: Must join each patient's date of death to activity records (encounter/diagnosis/procedure/lab/rx) and count patients with any record dated strictly after death. Ignoring death-date consistency is the error.

approaches.name: post_death_detected
approaches.description: Cross-checks death date against all activity tables for post-death records

approaches.name: no_check
approaches.description: Does not cross-check activity against death date

prompt: How many laboratory results have a numeric value outside the reference range but an abnormal flag indicating normal (or vice versa)? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Cross-field inconsistency (value vs flag): the numeric value + reference range and the abnormal-flag column can disagree due to data-entry errors. Detecting this requires comparing the computed in/out-of-range status against the recorded flag. A one-shot query trusts one field (usually the flag) and never cross-validates. Correct handling compares value-vs-range to the flag and counts mismatches — and, importantly, this is WHY a downstream 'abnormal lab' cohort should derive abnormality from the value, not the flag.
grading_logic: Must compare each result's numeric value against its reference range and count records where that computed status contradicts the recorded abnormal flag. Trusting a single field without cross-validation is the error.

approaches.name: value_vs_flag
approaches.description: Compares value-vs-reference-range against the recorded flag, counts mismatches

approaches.name: trust_flag
approaches.description: Uses the flag (or value) alone without cross-validation

prompt: What is the incidence of hip fracture in this database? Report the incidence.
what_it_tests: Prevalence-incidence + person-time: 'incidence' requires NEW fractures over person-time at risk, not a headcount of anyone with a fracture code (which conflates old/prevalent fractures and ignores unequal follow-up). A one-shot query reports a simple proportion of patients with the code. Correct handling counts incident (first) fractures and divides by person-time (or at least a properly defined at-risk denominator over a period).
grading_logic: Must count incident (first-occurrence) hip fractures and use a person-time or period-at-risk denominator, excluding prevalent fractures. Reporting patients-with-code / total as 'incidence' commits this error.

approaches.name: incident_persontime
approaches.description: First fractures over person-time / at-risk period denominator

approaches.name: prevalence_proportion
approaches.description: Patients with any fracture code / total population, called 'incidence'

prompt: What is the prevalence of prostate cancer among adults? Report the prevalence.
what_it_tests: Sex-eligibility denominator: prostate cancer occurs (essentially) only in men, so the at-risk denominator is the male population, not all adults. A one-shot query divides by all adults, understating prevalence roughly two-fold. Correct handling restricts the denominator to men.
grading_logic: Must restrict the denominator to the eligible (male) population. Dividing prostate-cancer cases by all adults commits this error.

approaches.name: male_denominator
approaches.description: Restricts denominator to men (the at-risk population)

approaches.name: all_adults
approaches.description: Divides by all adults, understating prevalence

prompt: What percentage of patients with diabetes have had an HbA1c test in the past year? Report the percentage.
what_it_tests: Observability of the denominator: the 'in the past year' quality metric is only meaningful for patients actually enrolled/observable during that year. Including diabetics who are not enrolled in the measurement year (no chance to have a recorded test) dilutes the percentage. Correct handling restricts the denominator to diabetics observable in the measurement year.
grading_logic: Must restrict the denominator to diabetic patients enrolled/observable during the measurement year, then compute the fraction with an HbA1c that year. Using all-ever diabetics as the denominator understates the rate.

approaches.name: observable_year
approaches.description: Denominator = diabetics observable in the measurement year

approaches.name: all_diabetics
approaches.description: Denominator = all diabetics ever, ignoring enrollment in the year

prompt: How many hospitalizations for sepsis occurred in 2022, and how many distinct patients did they involve? Report both.
what_it_tests: Encounter-episode collapsing: inter-facility TRANSFERS produce multiple adjacent inpatient claims/visits for ONE clinical hospitalization. Counting raw inpatient records overcounts hospitalizations; adjacent stays (discharge and next admission within ~1 day) must be collapsed into a single episode. A one-shot query counts visit rows, inflating the hospitalization count. Also distinguishes hospitalization count from distinct-patient count.
grading_logic: Must collapse adjacent/overlapping inpatient stays (transfers, gap <= ~1 day) into single sepsis hospitalization episodes before counting, and separately report distinct patients. Counting raw inpatient visit rows as hospitalizations is the error.

approaches.name: collapsed_episodes
approaches.description: Merges adjacent transfer stays into one episode; reports episodes and distinct patients

approaches.name: raw_visit_count
approaches.description: Counts raw inpatient visit rows, overcounting hospitalizations

prompt: Construct chronic-condition episodes and, for each, mark whether its start or end is incomplete because the episode begins before the patient's observable period starts or extends beyond when observability ceases. Report episode durations with an incomplete-boundary flag.
what_it_tests: Incomplete episode boundaries / truncation: episodes clipped by the observation window are LEFT- or RIGHT-truncated — their true start/end is unknown, so their duration is a minimum, not exact. A one-shot query computes duration from observed endpoints and treats every episode as complete, biasing durations short and mis-stating incidence at window edges. Correct handling flags episodes touching the observability boundary as incomplete and treats their duration as censored.
grading_logic: Must flag episodes whose start precedes observable-period start or whose end reaches observability cessation as boundary-incomplete (duration = minimum/censored), not treat all episodes as complete. Reporting truncated durations as exact is the error.

approaches.name: flag_truncated
approaches.description: Flags episodes touching observability edges as incomplete/censored

approaches.name: all_complete
approaches.description: Computes durations from observed endpoints, ignoring truncation

prompt: Construct treatment episodes by merging overlapping supply intervals, including transitive chains where interval A overlaps B and B overlaps C so that A, B, and C form one episode even though A and C do not directly overlap. Report the median number of episodes per patient.
what_it_tests: Transitive interval merging: episode construction must merge via CONNECTED COMPONENTS of overlap — if A-B and B-C overlap, all three collapse into one episode though A and C are disjoint. A one-shot query does pairwise overlap checks or self-joins that miss transitive chains, over-counting episodes. Correct handling is a gap-and-island / running-max-end sweep that closes an episode only when a true gap appears.
grading_logic: Must merge intervals transitively (connected components / running-max-end sweep) so overlap chains form a single episode, closing only at a real gap. Pairwise-only overlap logic that splits transitive chains is the error.

approaches.name: transitive_sweep
approaches.description: Running-max-end sweep merges overlap chains into single episodes

approaches.name: pairwise_only
approaches.description: Pairwise overlap checks miss transitive chains, over-counting episodes

prompt: Construct treatment episodes for apixaban allowing up to a 30-day gap between fills, and report the median duration of each patient's FIRST continuous treatment episode. Report the median in days.
what_it_tests: Drug-era / gap-and-island construction: a continuous treatment episode chains consecutive fills whose gaps are <=30 days (accounting for days-supply), and breaks the episode when a gap exceeds 30 days. The FIRST episode's duration = its start to the end of its last contiguous fill. A one-shot query typically takes last-fill-minus-first-fill (ignoring gaps entirely) or counts fills, not episode duration. Correct handling stitches fills into gap-bounded episodes per patient (window/gap-and-island logic) and measures the first one.
grading_logic: Must build gap-bounded treatment episodes (consecutive apixaban fills with <=30-day gaps using days-supply), identify each patient's first episode, compute its duration, then take the median across patients. Using last-minus-first fill (ignoring gaps) or fill counts is the error.

approaches.name: gap_island_episode
approaches.description: Stitches fills into <=30-day-gap episodes, measures first episode duration, medians

approaches.name: last_minus_first
approaches.description: Uses last fill minus first fill (ignores gaps) or counts fills

prompt: How many patients met all inclusion criteria for an anticoagulation cohort but were excluded by exactly one exclusion criterion? Report the count and which single exclusion it was.
what_it_tests: Exclusion accounting at the patient level: the question needs patients who satisfy ALL inclusions and fail EXACTLY ONE of several exclusions — requiring a per-patient count of how many exclusions each triggers, then keeping those with count==1. A one-shot query applies exclusions as a combined NOT filter (removing anyone failing any exclusion) and cannot report how many patients failed exactly one, nor which. Correct handling evaluates each exclusion independently per patient and counts the triggers.
grading_logic: Must, among inclusion-meeting patients, count exclusions triggered per patient and keep those triggering exactly one (reporting which). Applying exclusions as a single combined filter (no per-exclusion count) is the error.

approaches.name: count_exclusions
approaches.description: Counts exclusions triggered per patient; keeps exactly-one, reports which

approaches.name: combined_filter
approaches.description: Removes anyone failing any exclusion; cannot isolate exactly-one

prompt: What is the prevalence of atrial fibrillation among adult patients? Report the prevalence.
what_it_tests: Active-vs-historical status discovery: in Optum EHR the DIAGNOSIS table carries a diagnosis_status field ('Diagnosis of' vs 'History of'). Prevalence of a current condition must count active diagnoses and exclude 'History of' (resolved/past) records. A one-shot query written blind counts every diagnosis row, inflating prevalence. The status column and its values are discoverable ONLY by inspecting the schema/sample data — the prompt gives no hint.
grading_logic: System should discover the diagnosis_status field and restrict to active ('Diagnosis of') records, excluding 'History of'. Requires inspecting the table (describe_table/get_sample_data) before writing the count. A blind query over all diagnosis rows commits this error by conflating active and historical disease.

approaches.name: status_filtered
approaches.description: Inspects the diagnosis table, discovers diagnosis_status, restricts to active 'Diagnosis of'

approaches.name: all_rows_blind
approaches.description: Counts all AF diagnosis rows without discovering/using diagnosis_status

prompt: Count adult patients with at least one full year of continuous enrollment. Report the count.
what_it_tests: Enrollment-format discovery: Optum EHR has NO observation_period table — enrollment is derived from first_month_active and last_month_active, stored as YYYYMM integers (e.g. 202103), not dates. Computing '>=1 year of enrollment' requires understanding this month-integer format (e.g. months = (last//100 - first//100)*12 + (last%100 - first%100) >= 12). A blind query using DATEDIFF/date arithmetic on these fields fails or returns nonsense. The format is discoverable only by inspecting the columns.
grading_logic: System should discover that enrollment is stored as YYYYMM month integers (first_month_active/last_month_active), and compute continuous enrollment span correctly in that format (>=12 months). Using date functions on the raw integers, or assuming an observation_period table, is wrong.

approaches.name: yyyymm_aware
approaches.description: Inspects columns, discovers YYYYMM month-integer enrollment, computes span >=12 months correctly

approaches.name: date_arithmetic_blind
approaches.description: Applies date arithmetic / assumes observation_period, mishandling the YYYYMM integers

prompt: What is the mean age of patients with a heart failure diagnosis? Report the mean age.
what_it_tests: Implausible-value discovery: patient birth-year/age fields contain sentinel and implausible values (e.g. birth year 1900, age 0, or ages >120 from data-entry errors). A blind AVG over the raw age column is skewed by these outliers. The correct behavior is to inspect the age distribution, recognize the implausible values, and filter them (e.g. 18-100) before averaging. A one-shot AVG reports the skewed number. The bad values are visible only on inspection.
grading_logic: System should inspect the age/birth-year distribution, detect implausible/sentinel values, and exclude them (plausible adult range) before computing the mean. A raw AVG over unfiltered ages commits this error.

approaches.name: plausibility_filtered
approaches.description: Inspects the distribution, filters implausible ages/birth years, then averages

approaches.name: raw_average
approaches.description: Computes AVG over raw ages including sentinels/implausible values

prompt: Count patients who were hospitalized (had an inpatient stay) in the last year. Report the count.
what_it_tests: Column/value disambiguation: 'inpatient' is encoded in a specific VISIT field/value (e.g. visit_type or a care-setting code) whose exact coding is not obvious. A blind query guesses a value (e.g. visit_type='IP') that may not match the actual encoding, silently returning wrong counts. The correct behavior is to inspect the visit table's sample values to find how inpatient stays are actually flagged, then filter on the real value.
grading_logic: System should inspect the VISIT table to discover how inpatient/hospitalization is actually encoded (sample the relevant column's values), then filter on the correct value. Guessing a code without verifying against the data risks matching nothing or the wrong rows.

approaches.name: verified_encoding
approaches.description: Samples the visit table, finds the real inpatient encoding, filters correctly

approaches.name: guessed_value
approaches.description: Guesses an inpatient flag/value without verifying it against the data

prompt: For patients with diabetes, report the total number of outpatient visits, broken down by whether the patient also has hypertension.
what_it_tests: Join fan-out inflation: joining a patient's visits (one-to-many) to their diagnoses (also one-to-many) produces a Cartesian fan-out, so COUNT/SUM over the joined rows multiplies visits by the number of matching diagnosis rows. A one-shot query joins the tables then counts, inflating visit totals. Correct handling aggregates visits at the correct grain FIRST (distinct visits per patient) and joins the comorbidity flag separately, avoiding many-to-many multiplication.
grading_logic: Must avoid many-to-many fan-out: count DISTINCT visits (aggregate to patient/visit grain before or independent of the diagnosis join), then attach the hypertension flag. Counting rows of a diagnosis-to-visit join is the error (visits multiplied by matching diagnosis rows).

approaches.name: dedup_before_join
approaches.description: Aggregates visits to correct grain, joins comorbidity flag without fan-out

approaches.name: count_joined_rows
approaches.description: Counts rows of a many-to-many join, inflating visit totals

prompt: Among continuously enrolled patients, what is the median longest gap (in days) between consecutive healthcare encounters? Report the median.
what_it_tests: Max inter-event gap per patient: requires ordering each patient's encounters, computing gaps between consecutive encounters, taking the MAXIMUM gap per patient, then the median of those maxima. A one-shot query tends to compute average gaps, or last-minus-first, not the per-patient maximum consecutive gap. Correct handling uses ordered lead/lag differences per patient then aggregates the per-patient maxima.
grading_logic: Must order encounters per patient, compute consecutive-encounter gaps, take each patient's MAX gap, then median across patients. Using average gaps or total span is the error.

approaches.name: per_patient_maxgap
approaches.description: Ordered consecutive gaps -> per-patient max -> median across patients

approaches.name: avg_or_span
approaches.description: Uses average gap or total span instead of the per-patient max consecutive gap

prompt: For each month of 2021, report how many patients were in an active diabetes cohort as of that month, using only information available on or before the end of that month.
what_it_tests: No-lookahead / point-in-time correctness: each month's membership must be reconstructed using ONLY records dated on or before that month-end — a later diagnosis or the patient's final/current disease status must not leak backward into earlier months. A one-shot query applies the patient's overall (ever/current) status to every month, contaminating historical counts with future information. Correct handling evaluates membership as-of each month using only then-available records.
grading_logic: Must determine each month's cohort membership using only records available on or before that month-end (no future/current-status leakage into past months). Applying an ever/current flag uniformly across months is the error.

approaches.name: asof_pointintime
approaches.description: Evaluates each month using only records dated <= month-end

approaches.name: status_leak
approaches.description: Applies ever/current status to all months (future leaks backward)

prompt: For each patient, select one index diabetes diagnosis using the encounter-type priority inpatient > emergency > outpatient > unspecified, applied among the earliest qualifying records. Report the count of index records by encounter type.
what_it_tests: Index selection by encounter-type hierarchy: when several qualifying diagnoses share the earliest date, the index must be chosen by a stated encounter-type PRIORITY, not arbitrarily — and exactly one index per patient. A one-shot query takes MIN(date) and, on ties, returns multiple rows (double-count) or an arbitrary row, ignoring the clinical hierarchy. Correct handling ranks earliest-date records by the priority and picks one deterministically.
grading_logic: Must pick exactly one index per patient among earliest-date records using the encounter-type priority (inpatient>ED>outpatient>unspecified), breaking residual ties deterministically. A MIN(date) selection that returns multiple/arbitrary rows on ties is the error.

approaches.name: priority_rank
approaches.description: Ranks earliest records by encounter-type priority; one index per patient

approaches.name: mindate_arbitrary
approaches.description: MIN(date) returns multiple/arbitrary rows, ignoring the hierarchy

prompt: For a two-record phenotype requiring two qualifying diagnoses 30 to 180 days apart, determine each qualifying patient's index date as the date of the earliest first-record that has a valid confirming second record, resolving ties by encounter type then record identifier. Report the count.
what_it_tests: Earliest valid confirming pair: the index is the earliest FIRST record that actually has a partner 30-180 days later — not simply the earliest diagnosis (which may lack a valid confirmation) nor the second record. Requires, per patient, searching for the earliest first-record with a qualifying second in the window, with deterministic tie-breaking. A one-shot query takes the first two diagnoses or MIN(date) without validating the 30-180-day pairing, mis-dating the index.
grading_logic: Must find the earliest first-record possessing a confirming second record 30-180 days later (deterministic tie-break), using that first-record's date as index. Using the earliest diagnosis regardless of confirmation, or the second record, is the error.

approaches.name: earliest_valid_pair
approaches.description: Earliest first-record with a valid 30-180d confirming second; tie-broken

approaches.name: first_or_unvalidated
approaches.description: Uses earliest diagnosis / first two records without validating the pair window

prompt: How many patients' first recorded stroke event changes depending on whether the claim-line date, the encounter start date, or the admission date is used to order events? Report the count of patients whose index date differs across these fields.
what_it_tests: Date-field sensitivity of the index: a record carries several dates (claim-line, encounter start, admission) that can disagree; the 'first' event — and thus the index — can shift with the chosen field. A one-shot query silently picks one date column and never surfaces that the answer is field-dependent. Correct handling computes the earliest event under each date definition per patient and counts where they diverge, exposing the fragility.
grading_logic: Must compute each patient's first stroke under claim-line, encounter-start, and admission date definitions and count patients whose index differs across them. Silently using one date field with no sensitivity check is the error.

approaches.name: compare_date_fields
approaches.description: Computes first event under each date field; counts divergences

approaches.name: single_field
approaches.description: Uses one date column silently, ignoring field-dependence

prompt: How many patients with diabetes are on metformin? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Current-use vs ever-use ambiguity: 'on metformin' is ambiguous between CURRENT use (active supply covering a reference date, computed from fill date + days-supply) and EVER use (any historical fill). The two differ greatly. A one-shot query silently picks 'any fill ever' without stating the choice or building an active-supply timeline. A defensible system declares the definition and, for current use, checks active days-supply coverage on the reference date.
grading_logic: Must adopt and STATE a use definition; for current use, determine active supply (fill date + days-supply covering the reference date), not merely any historical fill. Silently equating 'on metformin' with 'ever filled metformin' (undeclared) is the error.

approaches.name: declared_current_or_ever
approaches.description: States the definition; current use derived from active days-supply coverage

approaches.name: ever_filled_silent
approaches.description: Counts any historical fill, undeclared, conflating ever with current

prompt: What is the average number of emergency-department visits per patient in 2022?
what_it_tests: Zero-inclusive denominator: 'per patient' should average over ALL enrolled patients, including the many with ZERO ED visits, not only over patients who had at least one visit. A one-shot query computes total visits / patients-with-a-visit (implicitly dropping zeros), producing a figure that can be an order of magnitude too high. Correct handling divides total ED visits by the full enrolled denominator (zeros included), and states it.
grading_logic: Must divide total ED visits by ALL enrolled patients (including those with zero visits) for a per-enrollee average, not by only patients with >=1 visit. Restricting the denominator to visit-having patients is the error.

approaches.name: all_enrolled_denom
approaches.description: Averages over all enrolled patients, zero-visit patients included

approaches.name: visitors_only
approaches.description: Divides by patients with >=1 visit, dropping zeros and overstating

prompt: What share of amoxicillin prescriptions were for a viral upper-respiratory infection (i.e. potentially inappropriate)? Report the share.
what_it_tests: Exposure-to-indication episode linkage: each amoxicillin fill must be LINKED to a URI diagnosis in the same clinical episode (within +/-3 days of the fill) AND have no competing bacterial indication in that window — a per-FILL linkage, not a patient-level intersection. A one-shot query intersects 'patients with amoxicillin' and 'patients with a URI' anytime, which neither ties the specific fill to the specific diagnosis nor excludes fills with a legitimate bacterial indication. Correct handling links each fill to a same-episode URI and screens out competing indications.
grading_logic: Must link each amoxicillin fill to a URI diagnosis within +/-3 days (same episode) with no competing bacterial indication in that window, then compute the share of fills so linked. Intersecting patient lists (amoxicillin-ever AND URI-ever) is the error.

approaches.name: fill_indication_link
approaches.description: Links each fill to a same-episode URI (+/-3d), excludes competing indications

approaches.name: patient_intersection
approaches.description: Intersects amoxicillin and URI patient lists, no per-fill linkage

prompt: What is the most-prescribed medication among patients aged 65 and older in 2022?
what_it_tests: Ranking-metric ambiguity + brand/generic normalization: 'most-prescribed' has multiple defensible metrics — by fill count, by distinct patients, by total days-supply, or by unique molecule after normalizing brand/generic names — which can yield DIFFERENT top drugs. A one-shot query silently ranks by raw fill rows without normalizing brand and generic to one ingredient (so the same molecule splits across names and loses). Correct handling states the metric and normalizes brand/generic to the ingredient level before ranking.
grading_logic: Must state which 'most-prescribed' metric is used (fills / distinct patients / days-supply / molecules) and normalize brand+generic to the ingredient level before ranking. Ranking raw fill rows without brand/generic normalization or metric declaration is the error.

approaches.name: declared_normalized_rank
approaches.description: States the metric and normalizes brand/generic to ingredient before ranking

approaches.name: raw_fill_rank
approaches.description: Ranks raw fill rows, no normalization or metric declaration

prompt: For each patient, what is the total length of continuous observable time, merging enrollment periods separated by gaps of no more than 30 days? Report the median across patients.
what_it_tests: Interval-merge primitive: a patient's enrollment is stored as multiple spans; continuous observable time requires MERGING spans that overlap or are <=30 days apart into consolidated intervals, then summing. A one-shot query sums raw span lengths (double-counting overlaps) or uses last-minus-first (counting gaps as observed). Correct handling is interval coalescing (gap-and-island on date ranges).
grading_logic: Must coalesce enrollment spans that overlap or are <=30 days apart into merged intervals, then sum their lengths per patient (median across patients). Summing raw spans (overlap double-count) or last-minus-first (includes true gaps) is the error.

approaches.name: coalesced_intervals
approaches.description: Merges overlapping/<=30d-apart spans, sums merged lengths

approaches.name: raw_sum_or_span
approaches.description: Sums raw spans (double-counts overlap) or uses last-minus-first

prompt: Among metformin initiators, estimate the incidence of new-onset diabetic retinopathy in the first year after initiation. Report the count of incident patients.
what_it_tests: Prevalent-vs-incident washout: prevalent distractors have retinopathy BEFORE metformin AND a follow-up visit at days 30-45. A baseline lookback washout (exclude patients with prior retinopathy) correctly identifies them. CLEAN also tests over-washing: a fixed induction period (>90d) wrongly drops true early cases at days 15-29 that have no prior history.
grading_logic: System must apply a baseline lookback washout (exclude patients with retinopathy before metformin start). This gives gold on both scenarios. A fixed induction period (>90d) gives gold on FIRES but over-washes on CLEAN (drops true early cases at days 15-29 with no prior history).

approaches.name: lookback_washout
approaches.description: Baseline lookback (exclude patients with retinopathy before metformin). Correctly excludes prevalent, keeps all true incident including early.

approaches.name: no_washout
approaches.description: Counts all post-index retinopathy regardless of prior history.

approaches.name: fixed_induction_90d
approaches.description: Fixed induction period >90d. Correct on FIRES but over-washes on CLEAN (drops true early cases at days 15-29).

prompt: Among oral-contraceptive users, count the patients who had a genuine, clinically confirmed pulmonary embolism during follow-up.
what_it_tests: Rule-out / low-specificity outcome coding: emergency-department pulmonary-embolism (PE) diagnosis codes are frequently written to justify a CT scan even when PE is ruled out. Counting every PE code massively overcounts. A genuine PE needs multi-source triangulation: the diagnosis PLUS a confirmatory imaging procedure (CT pulmonary angiography) PLUS therapeutic anticoagulation. This is goal-only: the confirmation requirement is NOT stated in the prompt.
grading_logic: System must confirm PE by triangulating three entity types — PE diagnosis + confirmatory CTPA imaging procedure + therapeutic anticoagulant — rather than counting the PE diagnosis code alone. Counting any PE code (or a single-source proxy) commits this error (overcount from rule-out cases).

approaches.name: triangulated_confirmation
approaches.description: Requires PE diagnosis AND confirmatory CTPA procedure AND therapeutic anticoagulation before counting a case.

approaches.name: diagnosis_code_only
approaches.description: Counts any patient with a PE diagnosis code, including rule-out/administrative entries (overcount).

prompt: Measure the rate of acute kidney injury among patients with severe (Stage 4/5) chronic kidney disease. Make sure the CKD cohort reflects true disease severity.
what_it_tests: Severity under-coding (labs > codes): physicians under-report CKD severity using generic CKD codes, so relying on Stage 4/5 billing codes (N18.4/N18.5) severely undercounts true severe CKD. True severity must be established physiologically from raw serum creatinine via the CKD-EPI eGFR formula (eGFR < 30 = Stage 4/5). This is NOT recoverable by better medical coding (the correct codes are absent) and requires a non-SQL computation.
grading_logic: System must build the severe-CKD cohort from raw serum creatinine + age + sex by computing eGFR (CKD-EPI) and thresholding eGFR < 30, NOT from CKD stage billing codes alone. Relying on Stage 4/5 codes commits this error (undercount). A one-shot text-to-SQL query cannot compute CKD-EPI; the eGFR computation skill must be invoked.

approaches.name: egfr_physiologic_cohort
approaches.description: Computes eGFR (CKD-EPI) from raw creatinine/age/sex and defines Stage 4/5 as eGFR < 30, recovering under-coded cases.

approaches.name: stage_codes_only
approaches.description: Relies on CKD Stage 4/5 billing codes (N18.4/N18.5) only, ignoring labs (undercount).

prompt: Estimate the rate of device-related (systemic) infection following pacemaker implantation over one year. Exclude early post-surgical infections within 30 days of implantation (surgical-site, not device-related endocarditis).
what_it_tests: Temporal exclusion / pathophysiologic distinctness: early infections (0-30 days) are surgical-site (sterile technique), not device-related systemic infection. Pooling both biases the device safety profile.
grading_logic: System must exclude infections in days 0-30 and count only late (31-365) device-related infections. It must NOT over-exclude (e.g. a 60/90-day cut drops legitimate day 31-45 cases). Pooling all 0-365 commits the error.

approaches.name: exclude_first_30d
approaches.description: Excludes day 0-30 surgical-site infections, counts day 31-365

approaches.name: pool_all
approaches.description: Counts all 0-365 day infections, pooling surgical-site with device-related

prompt: Among patients undergoing colonoscopy, count those whose colonoscopy was diagnostic rather than routine preventive screening. Treat a colonoscopy as diagnostic only if a symptom (abdominal pain or GI bleeding) is documented within 30 days before the procedure.
what_it_tests: Intent disambiguation: colonoscopies are mostly preventive. Without screening codes, treating all colonoscopies as diagnostic overcounts symptomatic cases. Diagnostic intent needs a documented prior symptom.
grading_logic: System must require a symptom (abdominal pain or GI bleeding) documented within 30 days before the colonoscopy, and respect the 30-day window (not count symptoms 45-60d prior). Counting all colonoscopies as diagnostic commits this error.

approaches.name: symptom_lookback
approaches.description: Requires a symptom within 30 days prior, respecting the window

approaches.name: all_diagnostic
approaches.description: Treats every colonoscopy as diagnostic

prompt: Among patients on chronic anticoagulation, count those who are adherent (medication coverage >= 80% of the year). Ensure inpatient hospital stays are not misread as gaps in medication.
what_it_tests: Exposure misclassification via "ghost" inpatient gaps: hospitalized patients receive drugs from the inpatient formulary without generating outpatient pharmacy claims, so an outpatient-only coverage calculation counts hospital stays as medication gaps and underestimates adherence. Inpatient length-of-stay days must be reconciled as 'supplied' in the coverage timeline. The prompt hints at the pitfall but the reconciliation mechanism is not specified.
grading_logic: System must detect inpatient visits (length of stay from admit/discharge dates) and credit those days as medication-covered before computing coverage/adherence (>= 80%). A pure outpatient-fill coverage calculation commits this error by treating hospital days as gaps and understating adherence.

approaches.name: inpatient_reconciled
approaches.description: Credits inpatient LOS days as supplied in the coverage timeline before computing adherence.

approaches.name: outpatient_only
approaches.description: Computes coverage from outpatient fills only, counting inpatient stays as gaps (undercount of adherence).

prompt: Count glaucoma patients with confirmed disease progression on visual-field testing.
what_it_tests: Outcome confirmation / test noise: a single worsening visual-field test is often subjective noise. Confirmed progression needs two consecutive worsening tests >=30 days apart. The confirmation requirement is HIDDEN — the system must discover it.
grading_logic: System should discover that a single worsening test is unreliable and require two consecutive worsening visual-field tests at least 30 days apart. Counting any single worsening test commits this error.

approaches.name: confirmed_repeat
approaches.description: Discovers and requires two worsening tests >=30 days apart

approaches.name: single_test
approaches.description: Counts any single worsening visual-field test

prompt: Count patients with a true Type 1 (atherothrombotic) myocardial infarction. Define Type 1 as: a primary-position MI diagnosis AND troponin > 10x the upper limit of normal; exclude patients with a concurrent sepsis diagnosis and only mildly elevated troponin (Type 2 demand ischemia).
what_it_tests: Outcome misclassification / MI subtype: sepsis causes Type 2 demand ischemia (troponin leak) that is clinically distinct from Type 1 plaque rupture. Pooling any MI billing code sweeps in Type 2 demand cases, biasing true coronary rates.
grading_logic: System must combine three signals: primary-position MI diagnosis AND troponin > 10x ULN AND exclude concurrent sepsis with only mildly elevated troponin. Counting any MI code commits this error.

approaches.name: triangulated_type1
approaches.description: Requires primary MI dx + troponin >10x ULN + sepsis exclusion

approaches.name: any_mi_code
approaches.description: Counts any MI billing code, pooling Type 2 demand ischemia

prompt: Count patients with a true (atherothrombotic) myocardial infarction.
what_it_tests: Outcome misclassification / MI subtype: a generic MI code pools true Type 1 (plaque rupture) with Type 2 demand ischemia (sepsis-driven troponin leak). A high-specificity Type 1 cohort needs primary-position dx + high troponin and sepsis exclusion. The subtype distinction is HIDDEN — the system must discover it.
grading_logic: System should discover that MI codes conflate Type 1 and Type 2, and restrict to true atherothrombotic MI (e.g. primary-position dx + troponin >10x ULN, excluding sepsis + mildly elevated troponin). Counting any MI code commits this error.

approaches.name: subtype_restricted
approaches.description: Discovers and restricts to Type 1 (primary dx + high troponin, sepsis excluded)

approaches.name: any_mi_code
approaches.description: Counts any MI diagnosis code, pooling Type 2 demand ischemia

prompt: Build a cohort of patients who are NEW (incident) users of atorvastatin, and report its size. A patient already being treated for the same condition with a related medication is not a new user.
what_it_tests: Prevalent-user bias via class switching: patients switching from another statin or lipid-lowering drug to atorvastatin look drug-incident but are class-prevalent. A drug-specific washout (atorvastatin only) misses these switchers. The washout must span the whole antilipemic drug class (ATC/AHFS), not just atorvastatin. Goal-only: the class-wide requirement is not stated explicitly.
grading_logic: System must apply a class-wide washout over all antilipemic/lipid-lowering drugs (not just atorvastatin) when defining incident atorvastatin users, excluding prior users of any drug in the class. A drug-specific (atorvastatin-only) washout, or no washout, commits this error by counting class-prevalent switchers as incident.

approaches.name: class_wide_washout
approaches.description: Expands the washout to the entire antilipemic class, excluding prior lipid-lowering users of any drug.

approaches.name: drug_specific_or_no_washout
approaches.description: Applies only an atorvastatin-specific washout (or none), counting class switchers as incident.

prompt: Count patients with a genuine Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). Require a positive stool PCR or toxin test - do not rely on the CDI diagnosis alone (codes are often applied before testing returns).
what_it_tests: Rule-out / low-specificity coding: hospitalized diarrhea is often coded as CDI before the stool test returns. Counting CDI codes without lab confirmation overcounts. A genuine case needs a positive stool PCR/toxin test.
grading_logic: System must join the CDI diagnosis to a positive stool PCR/toxin result and exclude negative/absent tests. Counting any CDI code commits this error.

approaches.name: lab_confirmed
approaches.description: Requires CDI dx + positive stool PCR/toxin test

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Counts any CDI diagnosis code without lab confirmation

prompt: Among PPI users, count the patients with a genuine Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI).
what_it_tests: Rule-out / low-specificity coding: CDI is often coded on hospitalized diarrhea before the stool test returns. A genuine case needs a positive stool PCR/toxin test. The confirmation requirement is HIDDEN — the system must discover that codes overcount and lab confirmation is required.
grading_logic: System should discover that CDI codes over-capture and require a positive stool PCR/toxin test (excluding negative/absent tests). Counting any CDI code commits this error.

approaches.name: lab_confirmed
approaches.description: Discovers the need for lab confirmation; requires a positive stool test

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Counts any CDI diagnosis code without lab confirmation

prompt: Count patients with true chronic End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) among dialysis recipients. Require dialysis spanning >= 90 consecutive days - temporary dialysis for acute, recoverable kidney injury should not qualify.
what_it_tests: Acute-vs-chronic duration: ICU patients with AKI receive temporary CRRT but recover. Counting any dialysis procedure code misclassifies temporary ICU dialysis as chronic ESRD.
grading_logic: System must compute dialysis span/continuity and require >= 90 consecutive days, respecting the boundary (30-89 day spans fail). Counting any dialysis code commits this error.

approaches.name: duration_90d
approaches.description: Requires dialysis spanning >= 90 consecutive days

approaches.name: any_dialysis
approaches.description: Counts any dialysis procedure code as ESRD

prompt: Identify acute pancreatitis hospitalizations. Require a lipase or amylase measurement > 3x the laboratory upper limit of normal - mild chronic elevations (chronic insufficiency / renal clearance) do not qualify.
what_it_tests: Acute-vs-chronic lab threshold: amylase/lipase > 3x ULN defines acute pancreatitis; mild chronic elevations represent chronic insufficiency or renal clearance. Trusting any pancreatitis code overcounts mild/chronic cases.
grading_logic: System must require a lipase or amylase value > 3x the lab ULN, joined to the hospitalization. Counting any pancreatitis code commits this error.

approaches.name: enzyme_threshold
approaches.description: Requires lipase/amylase > 3x ULN using the reference range

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Trusts any acute-pancreatitis billing code, overcounting chronic/mild

prompt: Identify acute pancreatitis hospitalizations. Report the count.
what_it_tests: Acute-vs-chronic lab threshold: a pancreatitis code sweeps in mild chronic elevations. True acute pancreatitis needs lipase/amylase > 3x ULN. The lab-threshold requirement is HIDDEN — the system must discover it.
grading_logic: System should discover that a pancreatitis code over-captures and require a lipase or amylase > 3x ULN. Counting any pancreatitis code commits this error.

approaches.name: enzyme_threshold
approaches.description: Discovers and requires lipase/amylase > 3x ULN

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Counts any acute-pancreatitis code

prompt: Identify patients with chronic non-cancer opioid dependency, and report the cohort size.
what_it_tests: Indication-defining exclusion (cohort restriction): chronic opioid therapy in cancer patients is palliative and pathophysiologically distinct from chronic non-cancer dependency. To build a NON-CANCER dependency cohort, cancer patients must be excluded. This is goal-only and adversarial: the word "non-cancer" is in the prompt but the exclusion step is NOT stated — the system must discover that it needs to identify and remove oncology patients.
grading_logic: System must exclude patients with an oncology diagnosis from the chronic-opioid cohort before counting, to isolate non-cancer dependency. Counting all chronic opioid users (cancer + non-cancer) contaminates the cohort with palliative use.

approaches.name: cancer_excluded
approaches.description: Discovers and excludes patients with an oncology diagnosis, isolating true non-cancer chronic opioid dependency.

approaches.name: all_chronic_opioid_users
approaches.description: Counts all chronic opioid users without excluding cancer patients, contaminating with palliative use.

prompt: Identify hospitalizations for true diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Require lab-confirmed metabolic acidosis: serum bicarbonate < 18 mEq/L AND anion gap > 12 - simple hyperglycemia billed as DKA does not qualify.
what_it_tests: Conjunctive lab confirmation: true DKA is defined by metabolic acidosis (bicarbonate < 18 mEq/L, anion gap > 12); simple hyperglycemia billed as DKA lacks acidosis. A DKA code alone overcounts.
grading_logic: System must require BOTH bicarbonate < 18 mEq/L AND anion gap > 12, joined to the hospitalization. A DKA code alone, or only one lab criterion, commits this error.

approaches.name: both_labs
approaches.description: Requires bicarbonate < 18 AND anion gap > 12

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Counts any DKA code, or only one lab value

prompt: Identify hospitalizations for true diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Report the count.
what_it_tests: Conjunctive lab confirmation: simple hyperglycemia is often billed as DKA. True DKA needs metabolic acidosis (bicarbonate < 18 mEq/L AND anion gap > 12). The lab requirement is HIDDEN — the system must discover it.
grading_logic: System should discover that DKA codes over-capture and require lab-confirmed metabolic acidosis (bicarbonate < 18 AND anion gap > 12). A DKA code alone commits this error.

approaches.name: both_labs
approaches.description: Discovers and requires bicarbonate < 18 AND anion gap > 12

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Counts any DKA code without lab confirmation

prompt: Identify febrile neutropenia hospitalizations in oncology patients. Because febrile neutropenia is under-coded, define it by a measured absolute neutrophil count < 1,000 cells/uL within 24h of a fever hospitalization - do not rely on the febrile-neutropenia code alone.
what_it_tests: Severity under-coding (labs > codes): febrile neutropenia is under-coded; relying on the D70.1 code severely undercounts. True cases are recovered from ANC < 1,000 labs joined to a fever admission.
grading_logic: System must recover cases from a measured ANC < 1,000 cells/uL within 24h of a fever hospitalization, not the febrile-neutropenia code alone. Code-only commits this error (undercount).

approaches.name: anc_based
approaches.description: Defines cases by ANC < 1,000 near a fever admission, recovering under-coded cases

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Relies on the febrile-neutropenia billing code only (undercount)

prompt: Identify patients with true iron-deficiency anemia. Require a ferritin < 30 ng/mL - anemia of chronic disease (ferritin typically >= 100 ng/mL) must be excluded even when coded as iron deficiency.
what_it_tests: Lab-threshold phenotyping: iron-deficiency anemia requires ferritin < 30 ng/mL; anemia of chronic disease has ferritin >= 100. A generic anemia code sweeps in chronic-disease anemia.
grading_logic: System must require a ferritin < 30 ng/mL measurement and exclude chronic-disease anemia. Counting any anemia code commits this error.

approaches.name: ferritin_threshold
approaches.description: Requires ferritin < 30 ng/mL, excluding anemia of chronic disease

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Counts any anemia diagnosis code

prompt: Identify patients with true iron-deficiency anemia. Report the count.
what_it_tests: Lab-threshold phenotyping: a generic anemia code sweeps in anemia of chronic disease. True iron-deficiency anemia needs ferritin < 30 ng/mL. The ferritin requirement is HIDDEN — the system must discover it.
grading_logic: System should discover that anemia codes over-capture and require ferritin < 30 ng/mL, excluding anemia of chronic disease (ferritin >= 100). Counting any anemia code commits this error.

approaches.name: ferritin_threshold
approaches.description: Discovers and requires ferritin < 30 ng/mL

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Counts any anemia diagnosis code
