prompt: Count patients with elevated natriuretic peptide indicating heart failure. Values come from two assays - BNP and NT-proBNP (by LOINC). Apply BNP > 100 pg/mL OR NT-proBNP > 300 pg/mL - not one threshold for both.
what_it_tests: Assay harmonization: NT-proBNP and BNP are different assays; NT-proBNP runs ~3-4x higher for the same heart-failure severity. Applying one threshold to both misclassifies.
grading_logic: System must split by assay (LOINC) and apply the correct threshold to each: BNP > 100 pg/mL, NT-proBNP > 300 pg/mL. A single threshold on all values commits this error.

approaches.name: assay_specific
approaches.description: Thresholds BNP and NT-proBNP separately by LOINC

approaches.name: single_threshold
approaches.description: Applies one cutoff to both assays

prompt: Count patients with definite infective endocarditis. Require BOTH positive blood cultures AND an echocardiogram - a diagnosis code alone is insufficient (many are suspected/rule-out).
what_it_tests: Conjunctive composite confirmation: definite infective endocarditis (Duke criteria) requires positive blood cultures and an echocardiogram showing vegetation. Many endocarditis codes are suspected/rule-out.
grading_logic: System must require BOTH a positive blood culture AND an echocardiogram procedure, joined to the endocarditis diagnosis. A code alone, or only one component, commits this error.

approaches.name: duke_composite
approaches.description: Requires endocarditis dx + positive blood culture + echocardiogram

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Counts any endocarditis code, or only one component

prompt: Count patients with a true recurrence of C. difficile. A recurrence is a second positive test/course 14-56 days after the first - <14 days is the same episode; >56 days is a new infection.
what_it_tests: Recurrence-window misspecification (temporal): a true CDI recurrence occurs 14-56 days after the first episode. Counting any second episode conflates same-episode continuation (<14d) and re-infection (>56d) with true recurrence.
grading_logic: System must compute the inter-episode interval and count only second episodes 14-56 days after the first. Counting any second episode (ignoring both bounds) commits the temporal error.

approaches.name: window_14_56
approaches.description: Counts only recurrences 14-56 days after the first episode

approaches.name: any_second_episode
approaches.description: Counts any second CDI episode, ignoring the 14-56d window

prompt: Build an Ankylosing Spondylitis cohort. Report the count.
what_it_tests: Under-specification / low-specificity coding: ankylosing spondylitis is frequently miscoded from generic inflammatory back pain. A high-specificity cohort must be confirmed by HLA-B27 positivity and absence of rheumatoid factor. Counting any AS diagnosis code overcounts. The confirmation requirement is NOT stated in the prompt — the system must discover it.
grading_logic: System should confirm AS beyond the diagnosis code — e.g. require HLA-B27 positivity and/or exclude seropositive (RF+) patients who are more likely to have a different arthropathy. Counting any AS code without lab confirmation over-captures.

approaches.name: lab_confirmed_as
approaches.description: Confirms AS with HLA-B27 positivity / excludes RF+ patients, not the code alone

approaches.name: code_only
approaches.description: Counts any ankylosing spondylitis diagnosis code

prompt: Count active acromegaly patients. Report the count.
what_it_tests:
Age-adjusted lab normalization: active acromegaly requires an elevated
IGF-1 above the AGE-SPECIFIC upper limit of normal (IGF-1 falls with age, so a
single flat cutoff misclassifies across ages). Counting any acromegaly code, or
applying a flat IGF-1 threshold, mis-captures. The age-adjustment requirement is
HIDDEN — the system must discover that IGF-1 reference ranges are age-dependent.
grading_logic:
System should confirm acromegaly with IGF-1 above the age-adjusted upper limit
of normal (per-age reference), not a flat cutoff and not the diagnosis code
alone. A flat IGF-1 threshold, or code-only, commits this error.

approaches.name: age_adjusted_igf1
approaches.description: Discovers IGF-1 is age-dependent and applies an age-specific upper limit of normal

approaches.name: flat_cutoff_or_code_only
approaches.description: Uses a flat IGF-1 threshold or the acromegaly code alone, ignoring age adjustment

prompt: Among patients with at least two blood-pressure readings per year for three consecutive years, what proportion had controlled blood pressure (<140/90) in ALL three years versus in ANY year? Report both proportions.
what_it_tests: Per-patient longitudinal aggregation vs row-level filtering: 'controlled in ALL years' requires aggregating each patient's readings PER YEAR, deriving a per-year control flag, then requiring all three years true — a patient-level operation. A one-shot query typically filters ROWS where BP<140/90 (row-level), which conflates 'has some controlled reading' with 'controlled all year' and cannot express ALL-years vs ANY-years. Correct handling groups per patient-year, then reasons across years per patient.
grading_logic: Must aggregate to a per-patient-per-year control status (e.g. all/most readings <140/90 that year), then compute (a) fraction of patients controlled in every one of the 3 years and (b) fraction controlled in at least one year — patient-level, not row-level. A row-level BP<140/90 filter is the error.

approaches.name: per_patient_year
approaches.description: Aggregates per patient-year control status, then ALL-years vs ANY-years per patient

approaches.name: row_level_filter
approaches.description: Filters rows with BP<140/90, unable to express all-vs-any per patient

prompt: For a diabetic cohort, report the median HbA1c value closest to each patient's index date (within +/- 90 days), using exactly one value per patient. Report the median.
what_it_tests: Windowed dedup with tie-break (one row per patient): each patient may have many HbA1c results near index; the metric needs the SINGLE result closest to index within +/-90 days, ties broken by most recent, then a median across patients. A one-shot query tends to take all in-window results (many per patient) and median over ROWS, over-weighting patients with more tests. Correct handling ranks per patient by |date-index| (tie-break recency), keeps the top one, then medians across patients.
grading_logic: Must select, per patient, the single HbA1c closest to index within +/-90 days (tie-break: most recent), then take the median of those one-per-patient values. Medianing all in-window results (multiple per patient) is the error.

approaches.name: one_per_patient_ranked
approaches.description: Ranks per patient by proximity to index (tie-break recency), keeps one, medians across patients

approaches.name: median_all_rows
approaches.description: Medians over all in-window HbA1c rows, multiple per patient

prompt: Among patients with at least four eGFR measurements over at least two years, how many had a sustained decline of 40% or more from baseline, confirmed by a second measurement at least 90 days after the first qualifying low value? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Confirmed sustained change, not a single crossing: a >=40% decline must be CONFIRMED by a second low measurement >=90 days later, so a lone transient low value does not qualify. A one-shot query flags any single eGFR that is >=40% below baseline (counting transient dips / lab error) and ignores the confirmatory-persistence requirement. Correct handling requires two qualifying low values >=90 days apart relative to a properly defined baseline.
grading_logic: Must require a >=40% drop from baseline CONFIRMED by a second qualifying measurement >=90 days after the first, per patient (not a single low value). Counting any single sub-threshold measurement is the error.

approaches.name: confirmed_sustained
approaches.description: Requires two qualifying low eGFRs >=90 days apart vs baseline

approaches.name: single_value
approaches.description: Flags any single >=40%-below-baseline value (transient dips counted)

prompt: Report the median baseline creatinine, defined as the measurement closest to the index date within the window from 180 days before to 7 days after index (inclusive of day +7).
what_it_tests: Asymmetric baseline window with boundary inclusivity: the baseline window is ASYMMETRIC (-180 to +7 days) and boundary-inclusive on the +7 side; 'closest to index' means the single nearest value (by absolute day distance), not the earliest, latest, or an average. A one-shot query uses a symmetric window, takes the pre-index or first value, or averages all in-window values. Correct handling selects the one measurement with minimum |days from index| within (-180, +7].
grading_logic: Must select, per patient, the single creatinine closest to index (minimum absolute day distance) within the asymmetric -180 to +7 day window (respecting boundary inclusivity), then median across patients. Symmetric windows, first/last value, or averaging in-window values is the error.

approaches.name: closest_in_window
approaches.description: Picks the nearest-to-index value within the asymmetric -180..+7 window

approaches.name: symmetric_or_avg
approaches.description: Uses a symmetric window / first-last / averages in-window values

prompt: How many patients have a sequence of three consecutive laboratory results with strictly increasing numeric values? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Strictly increasing consecutive triple: requires ordering each patient's results by date and finding three CONSECUTIVE measurements with strictly rising values — an ordered-sequence property, not 'has three results' nor 'max > min'. A one-shot query checks that a high and a low value exist, or counts patients with >=3 results, ignoring order and consecutiveness. Correct handling uses ordered lag comparisons over adjacent results.
grading_logic: Must order results by date and detect three CONSECUTIVE strictly increasing values per patient (adjacent-triple comparison). Checking only that >=3 results exist, or max>min, is the error.

approaches.name: consecutive_increasing
approaches.description: Ordered adjacent-triple check for strictly increasing values

approaches.name: count_or_extremes
approaches.description: Counts >=3 results / compares extremes, ignoring order & adjacency

prompt: Construct periods of laboratory abnormality that begin with the first abnormal result and end with the first subsequent normal result, and report the median duration of these abnormal periods.
what_it_tests: Abnormal-period construction: an abnormal period runs from an abnormal result until the NEXT normal result (which closes it); a patient may have several such periods, and a still-open period (no subsequent normal) is censored. A one-shot query measures span between first and last abnormal (ignoring interspersed normals) or treats each abnormal result independently. Correct handling walks the ordered results, opening on abnormal and closing on the first following normal.
grading_logic: Must build abnormal periods that open at an abnormal result and close at the first subsequent normal (multiple periods per patient; open periods censored), then median their durations. Using first-to-last-abnormal span, ignoring intervening normals, is the error.

approaches.name: open_close_periods
approaches.description: Opens on abnormal, closes on first following normal; medians durations

approaches.name: first_to_last
approaches.description: Spans first-to-last abnormal, ignoring intervening normal results

prompt: What proportion of emergency-department visits resulted in an inpatient admission on the same or the next calendar day? Report the proportion.
what_it_tests: Encounter linkage (ED -> admission): each ED visit must be linked to a subsequent inpatient admission occurring same-day or next-day for that patient. A one-shot query tends to check 'patient had an ED visit AND an inpatient stay' anytime, or joins without the same/next-day constraint, overcounting. Correct handling links each ED visit to an admission within the 0-1 day window per patient.
grading_logic: Must link each ED visit to an inpatient admission on the same or next calendar day (per patient) and compute the proportion of ED visits so linked. Any-time ED+inpatient co-occurrence is the error.

approaches.name: same_next_day_link
approaches.description: Links ED visit to admission within 0-1 day per patient

approaches.name: anytime_both
approaches.description: Counts patients/visits with ED and inpatient anytime

prompt: Report the distribution of patients by race/ethnicity category.
what_it_tests: Missing-category handling in a distribution: patients with missing/unknown race must be shown as their own category, not silently dropped — dropping them shrinks the denominator and inflates the percentages of the observed categories, misrepresenting the population. A one-shot query filters out NULL/unknown (or ignores it in the GROUP BY), so the reported percentages sum over a reduced base. Correct handling includes a 'missing/unknown' bucket and reports it against the full population denominator.
grading_logic: Must include a missing/unknown category and compute percentages against the FULL population (missing not dropped from the denominator). Silently excluding missing values (inflating other categories' shares) is the error.

approaches.name: missing_bucket
approaches.description: Reports missing/unknown as its own category over the full denominator

approaches.name: drop_missing
approaches.description: Excludes NULL/unknown, shrinking the denominator and inflating shares

prompt: How many diabetes patients completed individual monitoring components (HbA1c, lipid panel, eye exam, nephropathy screen) but never had ALL of them completed within a single 365-day window? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Monitoring-bundle completeness within a window: completing the bundle requires ALL components inside ONE rolling 365-day window; a patient may have every component at some point yet never all together in 365 days. A one-shot query checks each component ever (ANDing lifetime presence), counting such patients as complete. Correct handling searches for a 365-day window containing all components and flags patients who have each individually but never concurrently.
grading_logic: Must require all bundle components within a single rolling 365-day window to count as complete, and identify patients with each component present individually but never all within one 365-day window. ANDing lifetime component presence is the error.

approaches.name: window_bundle
approaches.description: Requires all components in one rolling 365-day window; finds never-concurrent patients

approaches.name: lifetime_and
approaches.description: ANDs ever-presence of each component, ignoring the concurrency window

prompt: Among patients who underwent total knee replacement, how many were later diagnosed with a prosthetic joint infection AND subsequently underwent a revision surgery? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Compositional multi-step cohort: the answer is an INTERSECTION of three sequential sub-cohorts — (1) knee-replacement procedure, (2) later prosthetic-joint-infection diagnosis, (3) still-later revision procedure. A one-shot pipeline tends to flatten this into a single filter and loses the sequential dependency (e.g. counts anyone with all three codes regardless of order/linkage). Correct handling requires decomposing into steps and chaining them per patient.
grading_logic: System must build the three sub-cohorts and intersect them per patient with the correct sequence (replacement -> later infection -> later revision), not just count patients who have all three codes anywhere. Flattening to a single co-occurrence filter is the error.

approaches.name: chained_subcohorts
approaches.description: Decomposes into replacement -> infection -> revision and chains them per patient in order

approaches.name: flat_cooccurrence
approaches.description: Counts patients having all three codes without sequencing/linking them

prompt: Of patients hospitalized for heart failure, what fraction were readmitted for heart failure within 30 days of discharge? Report the fraction.
what_it_tests: Compositional cohort with linked denominator: denominator = index HF hospitalizations; numerator = those with a SECOND HF hospitalization whose admission is within 30 days of the index discharge. Requires linking each index stay to its own discharge date and searching a per-patient window. A one-shot query that counts 'patients with >=2 HF admissions' ignores the 30-day linkage and the index/readmission pairing.
grading_logic: System must identify index HF hospitalizations, capture each one's discharge date, and count readmissions for HF admitted within 30 days of THAT discharge (per-patient, per-index linkage). Counting patients with multiple HF stays regardless of timing is the error.

approaches.name: linked_30d_window
approaches.description: Links each index discharge to a readmission within 30 days, per patient

approaches.name: any_multiple_admits
approaches.description: Counts patients with >=2 HF admissions, ignoring the 30-day linkage

prompt: Among patients who had an ischemic stroke, what fraction had a carotid imaging study followed by a carotid endarterectomy within 6 months? Report the fraction.
what_it_tests: Compositional cohort with ordered sub-steps: denominator = ischemic-stroke patients; numerator = those with carotid imaging AND a subsequent endarterectomy within 6 months of that imaging. A one-shot query flattens to 'stroke + imaging + endarterectomy present' and loses the ordering and the per-patient 6-month linkage.
grading_logic: Must anchor on stroke patients, then require carotid imaging followed by endarterectomy within 6 months of the imaging, linked per patient. Counting co-occurrence of the three without ordering/windowing is the error.

approaches.name: ordered_linked
approaches.description: Chains stroke -> imaging -> endarterectomy within 6 months of imaging, per patient

approaches.name: flat_present
approaches.description: Counts patients with all three regardless of order/timing

prompt: How many patients newly started on dialysis had at least one nephrology visit in the year BEFORE dialysis initiation? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Compositional cohort spanning a pre-index window: step 1 = identify dialysis initiators and their initiation date; step 2 = look back 365 days from THAT date for a nephrology visit. A one-shot query typically checks 'has dialysis AND has nephrology visit' anywhere in history, ignoring that the visit must precede initiation within a specific window.
grading_logic: Must find each patient's dialysis-initiation date, then require a nephrology visit in the 365 days before that date (per-patient pre-index window). Any-time co-occurrence is the error.

approaches.name: preindex_window
approaches.description: Anchors on dialysis start, requires nephrology visit in prior 365 days

approaches.name: anytime_cooccurrence
approaches.description: Counts patients with both dialysis and a nephrology visit anywhere

prompt: How many patients received chemotherapy? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Multi-source de-duplication: chemotherapy exposure appears across DIFFERENT tables — procedure claims (administration), pharmacy fills (oral agents), and administration records. A one-shot query typically checks one source (undercount) or unions sources but counts rows/appearances, double-counting patients present in several sources. Correct handling unions the sources and counts DISTINCT patients once.
grading_logic: Must capture chemotherapy across procedure, pharmacy, and administration sources and count DISTINCT patients (union, deduplicated), not patients-per-source or a single source. Single-source counting or double-counting across sources is the error.

approaches.name: union_distinct
approaches.description: Unions all chemo sources, counts each patient once (distinct)

approaches.name: single_or_double
approaches.description: Uses one source (undercount) or double-counts across sources

prompt: For each patient, determine the first date on which they had at least two, at least three, at least four, and at least five distinct recorded chronic conditions. Report how many patients reached each milestone.
what_it_tests: Cumulative multimorbidity milestone dates: each threshold's date is when the CUMULATIVE count of DISTINCT chronic conditions first reaches it — requiring ordering each patient's first-diagnosis dates per distinct condition and finding when the running distinct-count hits 2,3,4,5. A one-shot query counts total conditions ever (ignoring the running accumulation and its timing) or counts condition rows (not distinct conditions). Correct handling accumulates distinct-condition onset over time.
grading_logic: Must order each patient's per-condition first-diagnosis dates, track the running count of DISTINCT chronic conditions, and record when it first reaches each threshold. Counting total/ever conditions without the cumulative-over-time distinct logic is the error.

approaches.name: cumulative_distinct
approaches.description: Running distinct-condition count over ordered onset dates; milestone dates

approaches.name: ever_count
approaches.description: Counts ever/total conditions, ignoring cumulative timing & distinctness

prompt: Estimate the one-year incidence of gout among adults with at least one year of continuous enrollment. Report the incidence.
what_it_tests: Prevalence vs incidence: a pre-existing (prevalent) gout diagnosis is not an incident case and must be excluded via a baseline washout.
grading_logic: Any answer excluding prevalent cases passes (washout present). Including them fails (no washout). The washout axis determines pass/fail. The enrollment axis (baseline-only vs full 24mo) determines which acceptable answer — diagnostic but not penalized.

approaches.name: washout_baseline_only
approaches.description: Washout + 12mo baseline-only enrollment (all patients qualify)

approaches.name: washout_24mo_enrollment
approaches.description: Washout + 24mo total enrollment (excludes short-FU patients)

approaches.name: no_washout_baseline_only
approaches.description: No washout + 12mo baseline-only (includes prevalent with follow-up gout)

approaches.name: no_washout_24mo_enrollment
approaches.description: No washout + 24mo total enrollment (includes prevalent, excludes short-FU)

prompt: Count patients for whom NSAID use plausibly contributed to upper GI bleed within one year of starting the NSAID. Exclude cases where GI bleed is diagnosed within 60 days of starting the NSAID AND the patient had prodromal GI symptoms (dyspepsia/epigastric pain) before starting the NSAID (the NSAID was likely prescribed for the early symptoms of the bleed - reverse causation).
what_it_tests: Protopathic bias / reverse causation: when a patient has prodromal symptoms before drug start AND the outcome appears within 60 days, the drug was likely prescribed FOR the developing disease. These cases must be excluded as reverse causation.
grading_logic: System must check: (1) prodromal symptom before NSAID start AND (2) outcome within 60d. Both must be present to exclude. Boundary cases (within 60d but NO prodrome) are genuine.

approaches.name: protopathic_excluded
approaches.description: Correctly applies prodrome + 60d window exclusion. Keeps boundary cases (no prodrome).

approaches.name: no_exclusion
approaches.description: Counts all GI bleed within 1y. Includes reverse-causation cases.

approaches.name: over_exclusion_60d
approaches.description: Excludes ALL bleeds within 60d (regardless of prodrome). Wrongly drops boundary cases.

prompt: What is the rate of statin-induced rhabdomyolysis in the population? Report the rate.
what_it_tests: Wrong denominator: the at-risk denominator is statin-exposed patients, not the whole population. Rhabdomyolysis 'induced by statins' can only occur in patients who took statins.
grading_logic: The system must restrict the denominator to statin-exposed patients. Dividing by total population commits this error. We grade the numerator COUNT (10) to avoid penalizing rate-method choice (proportion vs person-time rate).

approaches.name: denominator_statin_exposed
approaches.description: Correctly restricts the denominator to statin-exposed patients. Rate = rhabdomyolysis among statin users.

approaches.name: denominator_all_patients
approaches.description: Uses the whole population as denominator. Understates the drug-induced rate.

prompt: What is the prevalence of diabetic retinopathy in the population? Report the prevalence.
what_it_tests: Wrong denominator / disease-specific complication: diabetic retinopathy can only occur in diabetic patients, so the denominator must be restricted to diabetics. A system that divides by total population commits this error.
grading_logic: System must restrict denominator to diabetic patients. Numerator = patients with diabetic retinopathy codes among diabetics.

approaches.name: denominator_diabetics
approaches.description: Correctly restricts to diabetic population. Prevalence = retinopathy / diabetics.

approaches.name: denominator_all_patients
approaches.description: Uses total population as denominator. Under-estimates prevalence.

prompt: What is the rate of contrast-induced nephropathy in the population? Report the rate.
what_it_tests: Wrong denominator: the at-risk denominator is patients who received IV iodinated contrast media (a transient procedural exposure), not the whole population. Contrast-induced nephropathy can only occur in patients exposed to contrast. Subtlety vs N2a/N2b: the exposure is a transient PROCEDURE, not a chronic condition or a drug, so it is harder to recognize as the denominator restriction.
grading_logic: System must restrict the denominator to patients who received IV contrast (CT/angiography with contrast). Numerator = acute kidney injury within 48-72h post-procedure among the contrast-exposed. Dividing by total population commits this error.

approaches.name: denominator_contrast_exposed
approaches.description: Correctly restricts the denominator to patients who received IV contrast; AKI counted only in that group.

approaches.name: denominator_all_patients
approaches.description: Uses the whole population as denominator, ignoring contrast exposure. Understates the rate.

prompt: What is the breast cancer screening completion rate among women aged 50-74? Report the rate.
what_it_tests: Wrong / multi-layer denominator: the eligible denominator is NOT all women 50-74. Standard quality-measure specs exclude women with (a) a prior bilateral mastectomy (no tissue to screen) and (b) an existing active breast cancer diagnosis (already diagnosed, screening is moot). The system must apply MULTIPLE clinical exclusion layers, not just demographic filtering.
grading_logic: System must exclude, from the denominator, women with a prior bilateral mastectomy AND women with an existing active breast cancer diagnosis, before computing the screening rate. Rate = screened / truly eligible. Applying only the age/sex filter inflates the denominator and understates the rate. (Only bilateral mastectomy excludes; unilateral does not.)

approaches.name: multi_layer_exclusions
approaches.description: Excludes both bilateral-mastectomy and active-breast-cancer women from the denominator (HEDIS/NQF-compliant), beyond basic demographics.

approaches.name: demographics_only
approaches.description: Uses all women 50-74 as denominator, applying no clinical exclusions.

approaches.name: partial_exclusion
approaches.description: Applies only one exclusion layer (e.g. mastectomy but not active cancer). Still commits this error on the missed layer.

prompt: Measure the cervical-cancer screening rate among adult women. Exclude women with a prior total hysterectomy from the denominator (no cervix → not eligible for screening).
what_it_tests: Ineligibility by prior anatomic status: women who had a total hysterectomy are ineligible for cervical cancer screening. Missing this exclusion understates the screening rate by inflating the denominator with women who cannot be screened.
grading_logic: System must exclude, from the denominator, women with documented absence of the cervix before computing the screening rate. Evidence of cervix absence may come from a procedure (total/complete hysterectomy — a partial/supracervical/subtotal hysterectomy leaves the cervix and does NOT qualify) OR an anatomical-status diagnosis (acquired/congenital absence of cervix). Rate = screened / eligible. Missing the exclusion inflates the denominator. The pass/fail axis is whether cervix-absent women are excluded at all — not the specific evidence source used.

approaches.name: cervix_absent_excluded
approaches.description: Correctly excludes women with documented absence of the cervix (total hysterectomy procedure or anatomical-status diagnosis) from the denominator (HEDIS/eCQM-compliant)

approaches.name: no_exclusion_all_women
approaches.description: Uses all women in denominator, ignoring hysterectomy status

prompt: Build a cohort of new users of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs). Require at least 365 days of continuous prior observation before the first fill to confirm no earlier use. Count the number of eligible new users.
what_it_tests: New-user look-back / baseline observability: to confirm a patient is truly a new user, the system must verify >=365 days of prior observation AND no prior drug fills in that window. Patients with insufficient look-back have unknown prior status and must be excluded.
grading_logic: System must require >=365d prior observation (first_month_active to first fill) AND no prior PPI in that window. Patients with short look-back are not confirmable new users.

approaches.name: lookback_enforced
approaches.description: Requires >=365d prior obs AND no prior PPI. Correctly excludes short-lookback and prior users.

approaches.name: first_fill_equals_new
approaches.description: First observed fill = new user, ignores look-back adequacy. Includes short-lookback patients.

approaches.name: all_patients_with_ppi
approaches.description: Any patient with a PPI fill, no new-user definition at all.

prompt: Estimate the one-year incidence of new-onset type 2 diabetes after statin initiation. Only include patients observed for the full 365-day window (or who had the event within that window); do not count unobserved time as event-free.
what_it_tests: Follow-up sufficiency / immature outcome window: patients with insufficient post-index follow-up (data cut before 365d) must be excluded from the denominator unless they had the event. Counting them as event-free dilutes the incidence (understates risk).
grading_logic: System must require full 365-day follow-up OR event within window. Patients whose observation ends before 365d without an event are NOT event-free — they are unobserved and must be excluded from the denominator.

approaches.name: full_fu_required
approaches.description: Correctly restricts to patients with ≥365d follow-up or event within window

approaches.name: all_initiators_denominator
approaches.description: Uses all statin initiators in denominator, treating unobserved time as event-free

prompt: Define each patient's index date as the first qualifying diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis that occurs during active enrollment and is a confirmed (not rule-out or history-of) diagnosis, then count patients who had a corticosteroid prescription in the 180 days before index.
what_it_tests: Index/anchor-date misspecification: the system must anchor on the first confirmed, enrolled diagnosis record — not MIN(date) over all rows (which picks up rule-out codes or pre-enrollment records). A wrong anchor shifts the 180d baseline window.
grading_logic: System must filter on diagnosis_status='confirmed' AND diag_date >= enrollment start. Wrong anchor shifts the 180d baseline window, over-counting corticosteroid use.

approaches.name: correct_anchor
approaches.description: Anchors on first confirmed enrolled RA dx. Correct 180d baseline window.

approaches.name: min_date_anchor
approaches.description: Anchors on MIN(date) of any RA code. Shifted baseline window picks up extra corticosteroid from rule-out patients.

prompt: Among patients in the cohort, report the proportion WITHOUT comorbidity Z at baseline. Only classify a patient as comorbidity-negative if they were observable at baseline (sufficient enrollment); do not infer 'negative' from patients with no baseline observation.
what_it_tests: Absence of record != absence of condition: treating patients with no baseline observation as comorbidity-negative overstates the healthy/negative fraction. Only observable patients can be classified negative.
grading_logic: System must restrict the negative classification to patients observable at baseline (sufficient enrollment); unobserved patients are unknown and excluded, not counted as negative. Treating no-code as negative for everyone commits this error.

approaches.name: observable_only
approaches.description: Classifies negative only among baseline-observable patients

approaches.name: no_code_negative
approaches.description: Treats absence of a code as negative for all patients

prompt: Count patients with severe hyperglycemia (blood glucose above 250 mg/dL) at any measurement.
what_it_tests: Unit harmonization: glucose is recorded in mixed units (mg/dL and mmol/L). A raw threshold on the number (>250) misclassifies mmol/L records. 250 mg/dL ≈ 13.9 mmol/L. Also: biologically implausible values should be filtered.
grading_logic: System must convert mmol/L to mg/dL (×18.0182) before applying the 250 threshold, and filter biologically implausible values. Raw numeric comparison without unit checking commits this error.

approaches.name: unit_harmonized_implausible_filtered
approaches.description: Convert mmol/L, exclude implausible (>100 mmol/L), threshold at 250 mg/dL equivalent

approaches.name: raw_numeric_gt250
approaches.description: Raw value > 250 regardless of unit (misses mmol/L highs, includes implausible)

approaches.name: only_mgdl_records
approaches.description: Only considers mg/dL records, ignores mmol/L entirely

prompt: Build a cohort of new (incident) users of a statin, and report its size.
what_it_tests: Class-wide new-user washout: a patient switching between statins (e.g. simvastatin -> atorvastatin) looks drug-incident but is class-prevalent. The washout must span the whole statin CLASS, not a single agent. Requires expanding 'statin' to the full class (many NDCs) -> currently blocked.
grading_logic: Must apply a class-wide washout over all statins (no prior statin of any kind in the lookback) when defining incident users. Single-agent washout or no washout commits this error.

approaches.name: class_wide_washout
approaches.description: Class-wide statin washout; excludes prior users of any statin

approaches.name: single_or_none
approaches.description: Single-agent or no washout, counting switchers as incident

prompt: What fraction of patients on antihypertensive therapy are adherent (proportion of days covered >= 0.8) in the year after initiation? Report the fraction.
what_it_tests: Class-level adherence with overlap handling: PDC for 'antihypertensive therapy' spans a broad drug class; overlapping fills must be shifted forward (not double-counted), and inpatient days credited. Requires class expansion (many NDCs) plus gap/overlap logic -> blocked today.
grading_logic: Must expand the antihypertensive class, build a covered-days timeline shifting overlapping fills forward (and crediting inpatient days), compute PDC over 365 days, and count PDC>=0.8. Naive fill-count adherence or double-counting overlaps is the error.

approaches.name: pdc_overlap_shift
approaches.description: Class-level covered-days with forward-shifted overlaps; PDC>=0.8

approaches.name: naive_adherence
approaches.description: Fill counts or double-counted overlapping days

prompt: Among new users of an SSRI, what proportion switched to an SNRI (rather than adding one) within 12 months? Report the proportion.
what_it_tests: Switch-vs-augmentation across two drug CLASSES: a switch = SSRI stops when SNRI starts; augmentation = both continue concurrently. Distinguishing them needs a 30-day overlap rule and expansion of BOTH classes (SSRI, SNRI) -> many NDCs -> blocked. A one-shot query also cannot express switch vs add.
grading_logic: Must expand both SSRI and SNRI classes, and classify as a SWITCH only when the SSRI is discontinued around the SNRI start (<=30-day overlap), not augmentation. Counting anyone on both, or ignoring the overlap rule, is the error.

approaches.name: switch_overlap_rule
approaches.description: Class expansion + 30-day overlap rule to separate switch from augmentation

approaches.name: both_drugs
approaches.description: Counts patients on both classes, ignoring switch-vs-add

prompt: What is the rate of statin-associated myopathy in the population? Report the rate.
what_it_tests: Drug-class exposure denominator: statin-associated myopathy can only occur in statin users, so the at-risk denominator is statin-exposed patients (the whole class), not the whole population. Requires expanding 'statin' to the full class (many NDCs) -> blocked. Dividing by total population commits this error.
grading_logic: Must restrict the denominator to statin-exposed patients (class-wide) and count myopathy among them. Dividing by the total population commits this error.

approaches.name: class_exposed_denom
approaches.description: Denominator = statin-exposed (class-wide)

approaches.name: all_population
approaches.description: Denominator = whole population

prompt: How many patients received pembrolizumab as their first line of therapy? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Line-of-therapy construction: 'first line' requires building regimens from drug administrations, collapsing co-initiated agents (within ~28 days) into one line, ordering lines, and taking line 1 — not merely 'ever received pembrolizumab'. Even for a single agent, correctly attributing it to 1L requires LoT logic. (Marked drug-class/LoT; regimen partners may span classes -> safest to run post-fix.)
grading_logic: Must construct lines of therapy (collapse co-initiated agents into a regimen, order lines) and count patients whose FIRST line contains pembrolizumab. Counting anyone ever exposed to pembrolizumab, ignoring line assignment, is the error.

approaches.name: lot_first_line
approaches.description: Builds LoT regimens and restricts to first-line pembrolizumab

approaches.name: ever_exposed
approaches.description: Counts any pembrolizumab exposure regardless of line

prompt: How many older adults are on concurrent therapy with three or more anticholinergic medications? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Class-level concurrency / polypharmacy: counts patients with >=3 DISTINCT anticholinergic drugs whose supplied intervals OVERLAP in time. Requires expanding the anticholinergic class (many agents/NDCs) and computing temporal overlap of >=3 distinct fills -> blocked today. A one-shot query counts anyone with >=3 anticholinergic fills ever, ignoring concurrency.
grading_logic: Must expand the anticholinergic class and require >=3 DISTINCT agents with concurrently overlapping supply among older adults. Counting >=3 fills anytime (no overlap, or same agent) is the error.

approaches.name: concurrent_distinct
approaches.description: Requires >=3 distinct anticholinergics with overlapping supply

approaches.name: anytime_fills
approaches.description: Counts >=3 anticholinergic fills anytime, ignoring concurrency/distinctness

prompt: Among patients with hypertension, how many have never had an abnormal potassium result? Report the count, and separately report how many have no potassium measurement at all.
what_it_tests: Never-abnormal vs never-measured: 'never had an abnormal potassium' is ambiguous with the absence of testing — a patient with ZERO potassium labs is not the same as one tested and always normal. A one-shot query lumps never-measured patients into 'never abnormal', silently treating missing data as normal and inflating the count. Correct handling separates three groups: tested-and-always-normal, tested-with-an-abnormal, and never-tested (reported as its own bucket).
grading_logic: Must distinguish never-abnormal-BUT-tested from never-MEASURED (zero potassium labs), reporting never-tested as a separate bucket rather than counting them as 'never abnormal'. Treating absence of testing as a normal result is the error.

approaches.name: separate_untested
approaches.description: Separates tested-always-normal from never-measured (own bucket)

approaches.name: missing_as_normal
approaches.description: Counts never-measured patients as 'never abnormal' (missing = normal)

prompt: Among patients with newly diagnosed epilepsy who started an antiepileptic drug, what percentage achieved seizure freedom (no recorded seizure) within one year of starting therapy? Report the percentage.
what_it_tests: Absence-of-event-in-window as a positive outcome: 'seizure freedom' = NO seizure code in the 1-year window AFTER AED initiation, among patients OBSERVABLE for that full year. This is temporal negation over an observable window. A one-shot query tends to count patients with a seizure (the opposite), or treats patients lost to follow-up as event-free, or ignores the post-initiation window. Correct handling requires full-year observability and the ABSENCE of a seizure in that window.
grading_logic: Must define the numerator as patients with NO seizure code in the 365 days after AED start, restricted to patients observable for that full year (not lost to follow-up). Counting seizures, or treating unobserved patients as seizure-free, is the error.

approaches.name: absence_observable
approaches.description: No seizure in the post-init year among fully observed patients

approaches.name: event_or_unobserved
approaches.description: Counts seizures, or counts unobserved patients as seizure-free

prompt: What is the median duration of chronic-condition treatment episodes, where episodes still ongoing at the end of the data have no recorded end date? Report the median in days.
what_it_tests: Open-ended interval handling: episodes with a NULL/absent end date are still ONGOING, not zero-length or erroneous. Duration math on a NULL end silently drops those rows (NULL arithmetic) or treats them as instantaneous, biasing the median toward shorter, completed episodes. Correct handling censors open episodes at the data cut-off (or last activity date) and includes them, acknowledging they are minimum durations. A one-shot query computes end-minus-start, losing every ongoing episode.
grading_logic: Must impute an end for open (NULL-end) episodes at the data cut-off / last-activity date and include them (as censored/minimum durations), not drop them or treat them as zero. Letting NULL-end arithmetic silently exclude ongoing episodes is the error.

approaches.name: censor_at_cutoff
approaches.description: Censors open episodes at data end and includes them in the duration set

approaches.name: null_dropped
approaches.description: end-minus-start drops NULL-end (ongoing) episodes or zeroes them

prompt: What fraction of patients received a statin within 90 days of their first ASCVD diagnosis? Report the fraction.
what_it_tests: Exposure-opportunity denominator: the denominator must be restricted to patients ENROLLED for the full 90-day opportunity window after first ASCVD diagnosis — a patient who disenrolls on day 20 had no chance to be observed filling a statin and biases the fraction downward if kept. A one-shot query uses all ASCVD patients as the denominator regardless of whether they were observable for 90 days.
grading_logic: Must restrict the denominator to first-ASCVD patients enrolled for the full 90-day post-diagnosis window (observable), then compute the fraction with a statin fill in that window. Using all ASCVD patients regardless of follow-up observability is the error.

approaches.name: observable_denominator
approaches.description: Denominator = first-ASCVD patients observable for the full 90-day window

approaches.name: all_ascvd
approaches.description: Denominator = all ASCVD patients regardless of 90-day observability

prompt: How many patients alternated between controlled and uncontrolled diabetes (by HbA1c) at least three times? Report the count.
what_it_tests: State oscillation detection: 'alternated at least three times' means the ordered state sequence has >=3 transitions between the two states — requiring ordered per-patient state records and counting actual switches, not merely presence of both states. A one-shot query counts patients who have both a controlled and an uncontrolled result (which needs only one of each), vastly over-counting. Correct handling orders states over time and counts transitions.
grading_logic: Must order each patient's control-state records over time and count patients with >=3 transitions between states. Counting patients who merely have both states present is the error.

approaches.name: count_transitions
approaches.description: Orders states; counts patients with >=3 actual state switches

approaches.name: both_present
approaches.description: Counts patients having both states at all, ignoring transition count

prompt: How many patients on warfarin had a gastrointestinal bleed while also taking an NSAID? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Event-during-overlap window: the GI bleed must occur DURING a period of concurrent warfarin+NSAID exposure (>=14 overlapping supplied days), not merely anytime in a patient who ever took both. A one-shot query checks 'has warfarin AND NSAID AND GI bleed' anywhere, ignoring that the bleed must fall inside the co-exposure overlap window. Correct handling computes the overlap interval from days-supply and requires the bleed within it.
grading_logic: Must compute the concurrent warfarin+NSAID overlap window (from fill dates + days-supply) and count GI bleeds occurring WITHIN that overlap, per patient. Counting patients with all three anytime, ignoring the overlap window, is the error.

approaches.name: bleed_in_overlap
approaches.description: Requires the GI bleed within the concurrent warfarin+NSAID overlap window

approaches.name: anytime_all_three
approaches.description: Counts patients with warfarin, NSAID, and a bleed anytime

prompt: Build a cohort of patients who are new (incident) recipients of chronic hemodialysis, and report its size.
what_it_tests: Baseline observability / new-user look-back, procedure-anchored: to call a dialysis recipient 'new', the system must confirm no prior dialysis AND require adequate prior observation (>=365 days of enrollment before the first dialysis). Patients with a first OBSERVED dialysis but insufficient look-back may be prevalent recipients whose earlier procedures are simply unobserved (left-truncation). The look-back requirement is HIDDEN — the system must discover it.
grading_logic: System should require >=365 days of continuous prior observation before the first observed dialysis AND no prior dialysis in that window, before counting a patient as a new recipient. Treating any first observed dialysis as 'new' (ignoring look-back) commits this error.

approaches.name: lookback_enforced
approaches.description: Requires >=365d prior observation + no prior dialysis before labeling a new recipient

approaches.name: first_observed_is_new
approaches.description: Counts any first observed dialysis as a new recipient, ignoring look-back

prompt: Estimate the one-year incidence of new-onset heart failure after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Report the incidence.
what_it_tests: Follow-up sufficiency / immature outcome window, procedure-anchored: patients whose observation ends before 365 days post-CABG without a heart-failure diagnosis are NOT event-free — they are unobserved and must be excluded from the denominator (or handled by censoring). Counting their unobserved time as 'no event' dilutes the incidence. The follow-up requirement is HIDDEN.
grading_logic: System should require a full 365-day post-CABG follow-up window (or an event within it), excluding patients censored before 365d with no event, or use a censoring-aware estimator. Using all CABG patients as the denominator and treating unobserved time as event-free commits this error.

approaches.name: full_followup_or_censor
approaches.description: Requires full 365d follow-up or event-in-window; excludes/censors those cut short

approaches.name: all_initiators_denominator
approaches.description: Uses all CABG patients as denominator, treating unobserved time as event-free

prompt: Type 2 diabetes can be identified by a qualifying diagnosis, a qualifying lab (HbA1c>=6.5), or a glucose-lowering medication. For patients who qualify, report which pathway qualified them FIRST (earliest qualifying date), and break down counts by that first pathway.
what_it_tests: Competing-pathway provenance: multiple independent definitions can each make a patient a case; the answer needs, per patient, the EARLIEST qualifying date across pathways and WHICH pathway that was — then a breakdown by first-qualifying pathway. A one-shot query picks one pathway, or reports overlapping per-pathway totals, and cannot attribute the earliest-qualifying source. Correct handling computes each pathway's first date per patient and takes the argmin.
grading_logic: Must compute, per patient, the earliest qualifying date under each of the three pathways, pick the minimum (the qualifying pathway), and break down patient counts by that first pathway (ties handled deterministically). Reporting per-pathway totals or a single pathway is the error.

approaches.name: argmin_pathway
approaches.description: Per-patient earliest date across pathways; attributes to the first-qualifying one

approaches.name: per_pathway_totals
approaches.description: Reports overlapping per-pathway totals or one pathway only

prompt: What is the median number of outpatient visits per patient in 2022? Report the median.
what_it_tests: Statistic over the correct unit of analysis: 'median visits per patient' requires FIRST computing each patient's visit count, THEN taking the median across patients. A one-shot query often takes a median/percentile over the visit rows directly, or divides total visits by patients (a mean, not a median), giving a different number. Correct handling aggregates to one value per patient before computing the percentile.
grading_logic: Must compute per-patient visit counts and then the median across patients (one value per patient). Taking a percentile over raw visit rows, or reporting mean visits/patient as the 'median', is the error.

approaches.name: per_patient_then_median
approaches.description: Counts visits per patient, then medians across patients

approaches.name: row_level_or_mean
approaches.description: Percentile over rows, or total/patients (mean) mislabeled as median

prompt: How many patients progressed through at least two successively higher chronic kidney disease stages (without an intervening lower stage)? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Monotonic ordered progression (state-machine over records): must order each patient's CKD stage records over time and detect a strictly non-decreasing advance through >=2 higher stages with NO intervening lower-stage record. A one-shot query typically checks 'has stage 3 and stage 4 anytime', ignoring order and intervening reversals. Correct handling reasons over the ordered stage sequence per patient.
grading_logic: Must order stage records per patient and require >=2 successive upward stage transitions with no intervening lower stage. Checking co-occurrence of two stages regardless of order/reversal is the error.

approaches.name: ordered_monotonic
approaches.description: Orders stage records; requires successive upward transitions, no intervening lower

approaches.name: cooccurrence
approaches.description: Counts patients with two stages present anytime, ignoring order

prompt: Assign each patient in 2022 to the provider responsible for the greatest number of their qualifying outpatient visits, resolving ties by the most recent visit then the lowest provider identifier. Report the number of patients attributed to each provider's specialty.
what_it_tests: Plurality provider attribution with deterministic ties: each patient maps to ONE provider — the plurality-visit provider — with a stated tie-break, so a patient is counted once. A one-shot query counts patient-provider pairs (a patient seeing three providers appears three times) or picks an arbitrary provider on ties. Correct handling ranks providers by visit count per patient, applies the tie-break, and attributes each patient once.
grading_logic: Must attribute each patient to their single plurality-visit provider (tie-break: most recent visit, then lowest provider id), each patient counted once. Counting patient-provider pairs or arbitrary tie handling is the error.

approaches.name: plurality_onetie
approaches.description: Ranks providers by visits per patient; deterministic tie-break; one per patient

approaches.name: pair_or_arbitrary
approaches.description: Counts patient-provider pairs or breaks ties arbitrarily

prompt: What is the point prevalence of COPD on January 1, 2023? Report the prevalence.
what_it_tests: Point-in-time denominator: point prevalence on a specific date counts, in the numerator, patients with a COPD diagnosis in a defined lookback (e.g. prior 3 years) who are ENROLLED on that exact date; the denominator is patients enrolled on that exact date. A one-shot query typically uses everyone with a COPD code ever / all patients, ignoring the on-date enrollment requirement for both numerator and denominator.
grading_logic: Must restrict both numerator and denominator to patients enrolled on 2023-01-01 (enrollment span covering that date), with the numerator having a COPD diagnosis in the prior window. Using all-time codes / all patients, ignoring on-date enrollment, is the error.

approaches.name: enrolled_on_date
approaches.description: Numerator and denominator both restricted to enrollment covering 2023-01-01

approaches.name: alltime_allpatients
approaches.description: Uses any COPD code ever over all patients, ignoring on-date enrollment

prompt: What is the prevalence of asthma in 2022? Report the prevalence.
what_it_tests: Prevalence-definition ambiguity: 'prevalence in 2022' can mean PERIOD prevalence (any asthma diagnosis during 2022 among those enrolled in 2022) or POINT/annual prevalence with a lookback (asthma dx in a prior window while enrolled). These give materially different counts. A defensible system states which definition it uses and applies matching enrollment; a one-shot query silently picks 'any code in 2022 / all patients' without acknowledging the choice or aligning the denominator.
grading_logic: Must adopt a coherent prevalence definition (period or point) and align the denominator to the enrolled population for that definition, stating the choice. Silently counting any asthma code in 2022 over all patients (mismatched denominator, undeclared definition) is the error.

approaches.name: coherent_definition
approaches.description: Picks period or point prevalence explicitly and aligns the enrolled denominator

approaches.name: any_code_all_patients
approaches.description: Counts any 2022 asthma code over all patients, undeclared/mismatched

prompt: What is the incidence of gout per 1,000 person-years over 2020-2022? Report the incidence.
what_it_tests: Multi-span person-time: patients often have MULTIPLE enrollment spans (disenroll then re-enroll). Person-years at risk must be SUMMED across all qualifying spans within 2020-2022 (and stop at the first gout event), not taken from only the latest/longest span. A one-shot query typically uses a single span or a naive max-min date range, mis-stating the denominator person-time.
grading_logic: Must sum at-risk person-time across each patient's multiple enrollment spans within the window (censoring at first gout, disenrollment, or window end), and count incident (first) gout. Using a single span or last-minus-first dates for person-time is the error.

approaches.name: summed_spans
approaches.description: Sums person-time across all enrollment spans, censoring at first event

approaches.name: single_span
approaches.description: Uses one span / naive date range for person-time

prompt: Calculate outpatient-observable person-time for 2022, excluding days each patient spent as an inpatient. Report total person-years.
what_it_tests: Person-time with carved-out intervals: inpatient stays must be SUBTRACTED from the observable interval, which requires interval difference (observable minus the union of inpatient episodes), handling overlapping/adjacent stays so no inpatient day is double-subtracted and no outpatient day is lost. A one-shot query subtracts a raw count of inpatient claims/days (double-counting overlapping stays) or ignores inpatient time entirely. Correct handling computes observable-interval minus merged-inpatient-intervals.
grading_logic: Must subtract the MERGED inpatient intervals from each patient's observable interval (interval difference), not a raw inpatient-day count, then sum remaining person-time. Subtracting raw inpatient claim days (overlap double-count) or ignoring inpatient time is the error.

approaches.name: interval_difference
approaches.description: Observable interval minus merged inpatient intervals (no double-subtract)

approaches.name: raw_day_subtract
approaches.description: Subtracts raw inpatient claim/day counts, mishandling overlaps

prompt: Split each patient's observable time across calendar month, calendar year, age group, and diabetes disease-status (pre- vs post-diagnosis) boundaries, and report total person-days by each combination without double-counting any day.
what_it_tests: Multidimensional person-time splitting: each observable interval must be cut simultaneously at month-ends, year-ends, birthdays, AND the diagnosis date, so every day belongs to exactly ONE (month, year, age, disease-status) cell with no day counted twice or dropped. A one-shot query splits on at most one dimension, or assigns whole intervals to a single cell, producing overlapping/duplicated or missing person-days. Correct handling intersects all boundary sets and verifies the day total reconciles.
grading_logic: Must split intervals at the union of month, year, birthday, and diagnosis boundaries so each day maps to exactly one multidimensional cell (total person-days reconciles to raw observable days). Splitting on one dimension or assigning whole intervals is the error.

approaches.name: full_multidim_split
approaches.description: Cuts at all boundary types; each day in exactly one cell; total reconciles

approaches.name: partial_split
approaches.description: Splits on one dimension / assigns whole intervals, duplicating or dropping days

prompt: Compute each patient's total observable person-days two ways — by expanding to one row per observable day and by summing merged date intervals — and report whether the two totals agree.
what_it_tests: Person-time method reconciliation: the daily-expansion total and the merged-interval total must AGREE only if overlapping enrollment spans are correctly merged and interval endpoints are counted consistently (inclusive/exclusive). Discrepancies reveal double-counted overlap days or off-by-one endpoint errors. A one-shot query computes one method (often raw interval sums that double-count overlaps) and never cross-checks. Correct handling implements both and reconciles, exposing overlap/boundary handling.
grading_logic: Must compute person-days by day-level expansion AND by summing merged intervals, then compare — agreement requires merging overlaps and consistent endpoint counting. Reporting a single method (esp. raw interval sums that double-count overlaps) with no reconciliation is the error.

approaches.name: two_methods_reconcile
approaches.description: Computes both daily-expansion and merged-interval totals and reconciles

approaches.name: single_method
approaches.description: One method only (raw sums double-count overlaps), no cross-check

prompt: Report total observed person-years by calendar year and age group, correctly splitting each patient's observable time when they cross a year boundary or have a birthday mid-interval. Report the grid.
what_it_tests: Person-time splitting across year AND age boundaries: a single observable interval must be CUT at each Dec 31 and at each birthday, allocating the right fraction of person-time to each (year, age-group) cell. A one-shot query assigns a patient's whole interval to one year/age (by index date or enrollment start), mis-allocating person-time. Correct handling splits intervals at both boundary types.
grading_logic: Must split each observable interval at calendar-year boundaries and at birthdays, attributing the correct person-time fraction to each (year, age-group) cell. Assigning the whole interval to a single year/age bucket is the error.

approaches.name: split_at_boundaries
approaches.description: Splits intervals at year-ends and birthdays; allocates fractional person-time

approaches.name: whole_interval_one_bucket
approaches.description: Assigns each interval to one year/age by index/start date

prompt: Report both the annual and the monthly counts of active heart-failure episodes for 2022, and reconcile them — an episode spanning multiple months must not be summed across months to equal the annual total. Report both plus the reconciliation.
what_it_tests: Cross-grain reconciliation: an episode active across several months is counted in EACH of those months, so summing monthly counts overstates the (distinct-episode) annual total. The system must compute annual as distinct episodes active in the year, monthly as episodes active per month, and explain the difference (episodes spanning months). A one-shot query reports one grain, or naively sums months to 'annual', producing an inflated, inconsistent total.
grading_logic: Must compute the annual count as distinct episodes active in 2022 AND monthly active-episode counts, recognizing that monthly counts sum to MORE than annual because multi-month episodes recur; the totals are reconciled, not equated. Summing months to get the annual total is the error.

approaches.name: reconciled
approaches.description: Distinct-episode annual + per-month active counts, reconciled (not summed)

approaches.name: summed_months
approaches.description: Sums monthly counts to the annual total, over-counting multi-month episodes

prompt: How many acute myocardial infarction events occurred in 2022, where events for the same patient within 30 days of each other count as a single event? Report the event count.
what_it_tests: Recurrent-event counting with a refractory window: the same clinical event generates repeat codes across days; a NEW event only counts if it is >30 days after the prior counted event for that patient. This differs from first-event-only (undercount) and from raw code counts (overcount). It also differs from episode-collapsing by adjacency — here re-qualification requires a fixed clearance gap. Correct handling walks each patient's ordered event dates, starting a new event only when >30 days have elapsed since the last counted one.
grading_logic: Must count recurrent events per patient where a new event requires >30 days since the previously counted event (collapsing codes within 30 days into one), allowing multiple events per patient. Counting all codes (overcount) or only the first event (undercount) is the error.

approaches.name: refractory_gap
approaches.description: Ordered event dates; new event only if >30 days since last counted

approaches.name: all_or_first
approaches.description: Counts every code (overcount) or only the first event per patient

prompt: How many patients qualified for a heart-failure cohort, stopped qualifying, and then re-qualified at least 180 days after they last stopped qualifying? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Requalification after a clearance gap: membership is a time-varying interval; requalification requires the patient to LEAVE the cohort and re-enter only after >=180 days of non-qualifying time. A one-shot query treats cohort membership as a static ever/never flag and cannot express leave-then-return, or counts anyone with two qualifying spans regardless of the 180-day gap. Correct handling builds per-patient qualifying intervals and detects a re-entry preceded by a >=180-day non-qualifying gap.
grading_logic: Must construct time-varying cohort-membership intervals per patient and count those with a re-entry occurring >=180 days after a prior exit. A static ever-qualified flag, or ignoring the 180-day gap, is the error.

approaches.name: interval_requalify
approaches.description: Builds membership intervals; detects re-entry after >=180d non-qualifying gap

approaches.name: static_flag
approaches.description: Treats membership as ever/never or ignores the clearance gap

prompt: For a single named maintenance medication (levothyroxine), reconstruct exposure when refills arrive before the prior supply is exhausted, carrying unused supply forward. Report the median continuous exposure duration.
what_it_tests: Refill stockpiling / carry-forward: early refills mean supplied days accumulate ahead of consumption; a correct exposure timeline shifts each fill's start to the end of the prior adjusted supply (carry-forward), rather than starting supply at the fill date. A one-shot query sums days-supply from raw fill dates (double-counting overlapping supply) or uses fill-date-to-fill-date. Correct handling adjusts each fill's coverage start for stockpiled supply.
grading_logic: Must build the exposure timeline by carrying forward unused supply (each fill's coverage begins when the prior adjusted supply ends), then measure continuous exposure. Summing raw days-supply over overlapping fills, or raw fill-date spacing, is the error.

approaches.name: carry_forward
approaches.description: Shifts fill coverage start by leftover supply (stockpiling-adjusted timeline)

approaches.name: raw_supply
approaches.description: Sums raw days-supply / uses raw fill dates, double-counting overlap

prompt: Report the distribution of the Charlson Comorbidity Index among patients hospitalized for pneumonia. Report the distribution.
what_it_tests: Composite clinical score from many components: the Charlson index is computed per patient by mapping ~17 weighted comorbidity categories (MI, CHF, dementia, diabetes, cancer, liver disease, etc.) from diagnosis codes and summing the weights. A one-shot query cannot assemble a 17-category weighted score in a single pass — it tends to count raw diagnoses or a single condition. Correct handling builds each comorbidity flag per patient, applies the Charlson weights, sums per patient, then reports the score distribution.
grading_logic: Must map the ~17 Charlson comorbidity categories from diagnosis codes per patient, apply the standard category weights, sum to a per-patient score, and report the distribution. Counting raw diagnoses or omitting the weighted multi-category composition is the error.

approaches.name: weighted_composite
approaches.description: Builds all Charlson categories per patient, applies weights, sums, reports distribution

approaches.name: raw_or_partial
approaches.description: Counts raw diagnoses or a subset without the weighted 17-category composite

prompt: Is there a seasonal pattern in new influenza diagnoses? Report the diagnosis rate by calendar month, pooled across 2019-2023.
what_it_tests: Seasonality with person-time / days-in-month normalization: raw monthly COUNTS conflate true seasonality with (a) unequal days per month (Feb vs Jul) and (b) changing enrollment/observable population by month/year. A one-shot query reports raw counts per month, implying a seasonal signal that is partly a denominator artifact. Correct handling divides monthly events by observable person-time (or population) that month, and pools rates comparably across months.
grading_logic: Must express each month as a RATE normalized by observable person-time/population that month (accounting for days-in-month and enrollment), not raw counts, before comparing months. Reporting raw monthly counts as the seasonal signal is the error.

approaches.name: person_time_norm
approaches.description: Monthly events / observable person-time (normalized for days & enrollment)

approaches.name: raw_counts
approaches.description: Raw counts per month, conflating seasonality with denominator size

prompt: Convert each patient's overlapping active chronic-condition periods into non-overlapping time segments, each labeled by the exact set of conditions active during that segment. Report the segment breakdown.
what_it_tests: Interval flattening into labeled segments: overlapping condition intervals must be cut at every start/stop boundary into disjoint segments, each tagged with the SET of conditions simultaneously active. A one-shot query cannot decompose overlapping intervals into a segment timeline; it reports per-condition durations that overlap and double-count time. Correct handling is a sweep-line / boundary-split over interval unions.
grading_logic: Must split the union of overlapping condition intervals at every boundary into non-overlapping segments, each labeled by the active condition set, so total segment time has no double-counting. Reporting overlapping per-condition intervals is the error.

approaches.name: boundary_split
approaches.description: Sweep-line splits overlaps into disjoint segments labeled by active condition set

approaches.name: overlapping_durations
approaches.description: Reports per-condition durations that overlap/double-count time

prompt: Count patients who had, in order, a qualifying diagnosis, then a confirmatory test, then a treatment initiation, all within a single 90-day window (unrelated events may occur in between). Report the count.
what_it_tests: Ordered subsequence within a window: the three events must occur in the specified ORDER and within 90 days of each other, but other unrelated events may interleave. A one-shot query checks co-occurrence of the three within 90 days without enforcing order, or requires them to be strictly consecutive records. Correct handling finds an ordered subsequence (dx < test < treatment) inside a 90-day span per patient.
grading_logic: Must require dx-date < test-date < treatment-date with the span from dx to treatment <=90 days, per patient, allowing unrelated intervening events. Ignoring order, or requiring strict adjacency, is the error.

approaches.name: ordered_subsequence
approaches.description: Enforces dx<test<treatment within a 90-day span, intervening events allowed

approaches.name: unordered_or_adjacent
approaches.description: Checks co-occurrence without order, or requires strict adjacency

prompt: How many patients completed a full 3-dose hepatitis B vaccination series, respecting the minimum required intervals between doses? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Dose-series construction with spacing rules: a valid series requires 3 doses in order with MINIMUM intervals between them (e.g. dose2 >= 4 weeks after dose1, dose3 >= 8 weeks after dose2 and >= 16 after dose1); doses too close don't count and same-day duplicates collapse. A one-shot query counts patients with >=3 vaccine records, ignoring spacing and duplicates. Correct handling walks the ordered doses applying the interval rules.
grading_logic: Must validate an ordered 3-dose series meeting the minimum inter-dose intervals (collapsing same-day duplicates, rejecting too-close doses). Counting patients with >=3 vaccine records regardless of spacing is the error.

approaches.name: spaced_series
approaches.description: Validates ordered doses with minimum intervals, dedups same-day

approaches.name: count_three
approaches.description: Counts >=3 vaccine records ignoring spacing/duplicates

prompt: Using the code-based, lab-based, and medication-based definitions of diabetes, report how many patients meet exactly one, exactly two, or all three definitions. Report the mutually exclusive counts.
what_it_tests: Mutually-exclusive set partitioning (no double-count): a patient meeting 2 definitions must be counted once in the 'exactly two' bucket, not in each. Requires computing per-patient membership across three definitions and partitioning by the COUNT of definitions met. A one-shot query tends to report each definition's total (overlapping) or a simple union, which double-counts and can't produce exactly-one/two/three buckets.
grading_logic: Must compute, per patient, how many of the three diabetes definitions are met, then bucket patients by that count (exactly 1 / exactly 2 / all 3) with each patient in exactly one bucket. Reporting overlapping per-definition totals is the error.

approaches.name: exact_partition
approaches.description: Counts definitions met per patient; partitions into mutually exclusive buckets

approaches.name: overlapping_totals
approaches.description: Reports per-definition totals or a union, double-counting

prompt: Among patients with any malignancy diagnosis, how many have non-melanoma skin cancer as their ONLY malignancy? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Patient-level set subtraction, not code-level: 'only malignancy is NMSC' means the patient has >=1 NMSC code AND ZERO codes for any other malignancy — a per-PATIENT condition over their full code set, not a per-code filter. A one-shot query filters to NMSC codes (keeping patients who also have other cancers) or subtracts at the code level, both wrong. Correct handling computes, per patient, the set of distinct malignancy types and keeps those whose set == {NMSC}.
grading_logic: Must identify patients whose ENTIRE set of malignancy diagnoses contains only non-melanoma skin cancer (>=1 NMSC and no other malignancy code), a patient-level set condition. Filtering to NMSC rows (ignoring patients' other cancers) or code-level subtraction is the error.

approaches.name: patient_set_only
approaches.description: Keeps patients whose full malignancy set is exactly {NMSC}

approaches.name: code_level_filter
approaches.description: Filters to NMSC codes, keeping patients with other cancers too

prompt: How many patients have chronic kidney disease stage 3 or worse? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Lab-based staging with repeated-measure confirmation: CKD stage 3+ is defined physiologically by TWO eGFR measurements < 60 taken at least 90 days apart (to establish chronicity), not by a single low eGFR and not by CKD stage billing codes (under-coded). A one-shot query uses stage codes, or a single eGFR<60 (which may be acute kidney injury, not chronic). Correct handling requires two qualifying eGFR values >=90 days apart per patient.
grading_logic: Must define CKD 3+ from >=2 eGFR measurements <60 at least 90 days apart per patient (chronicity), computing eGFR from creatinine if needed — not from CKD stage codes and not from a single low eGFR. Single-measurement or code-based definitions commit this error.

approaches.name: two_egfr_90d
approaches.description: Requires two eGFR<60 >=90 days apart per patient (chronic)

approaches.name: code_or_single
approaches.description: Uses CKD stage codes, or a single eGFR<60 (may be acute)

prompt: How many patients had at least three consecutive abnormal laboratory results with no normal result in between? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Consecutive-run / streak detection: must order each patient's results by date and find a run of >=3 abnormal results uninterrupted by any normal result. A one-shot query counts patients with >=3 abnormal results total (ignoring that a normal result in between breaks the streak). Correct handling is gap-and-island/streak logic over the ordered sequence.
grading_logic: Must detect a maximal run of >=3 consecutive abnormal results (ordered by date) with no intervening normal result per patient. Counting >=3 abnormal results anywhere (streak-agnostic) is the error.

approaches.name: streak_detected
approaches.description: Finds >=3 consecutive abnormals with no intervening normal (ordered)

approaches.name: count_abnormals
approaches.description: Counts >=3 abnormal results total, ignoring intervening normals

prompt: Report the prevalence of obesity by calendar year and sex for 2020-2022. Some patients have sex recorded inconsistently across years.
what_it_tests: Inconsistent time-varying attribute across strata: when a patient's recorded sex differs across years, naive stratification places the same patient in different sex strata in different years (or double-counts), producing incoherent sex-specific denominators. A one-shot query strata by the per-row/per-year value without reconciling. Correct handling resolves each patient to ONE sex (e.g. most-recent or modal, stated) and applies it consistently, or explicitly reports the inconsistency count.
grading_logic: Must resolve each patient's sex to a single value (stated rule, e.g. modal/most-recent) applied consistently across years, or flag inconsistent patients as a separate bucket — not let the same patient flip strata year to year. Stratifying by unreconciled per-year sex is the error.

approaches.name: reconciled_attribute
approaches.description: Resolves each patient to one sex (stated rule) applied across all years

approaches.name: per_year_flip
approaches.description: Uses per-year sex, letting patients flip strata / double-count

prompt: How many patients had four or more emergency-department visits within any rolling 90-day period? Report the count.
what_it_tests: Sliding-window maximum (not fixed calendar windows): 'any rolling 90-day period' means the window can start on ANY visit date, so a patient with 4 visits spanning day 10-95 qualifies even though no single calendar quarter contains all four. A one-shot query buckets by fixed calendar quarter/year and misses cross-boundary clusters. Correct handling checks, per patient, whether any visit-anchored 90-day window contains >=4 visits.
grading_logic: Must evaluate rolling 90-day windows anchored at each ED visit per patient (e.g. count visits within 90 days of each visit) and flag patients reaching >=4 in any such window. Fixed calendar-period bucketing is the error.

approaches.name: rolling_window
approaches.description: Checks visit-anchored rolling 90-day windows per patient

approaches.name: calendar_bucket
approaches.description: Buckets visits by fixed calendar period, missing cross-boundary clusters

prompt: Classify each patient's terminal state as death, end of observability (disenrollment), or end of available data, and report the distribution.
what_it_tests: Terminal-state classification: a patient's follow-up ends for one of three DISTINCT reasons — death, disenrollment, or the data cut-off — and conflating them (e.g. treating disenrollment or data-end as death, or all non-deaths as 'still followed') misrepresents censoring. A one-shot query typically has no notion of why observation stops. Correct handling assigns each patient exactly one terminal reason using the earliest applicable of death date, disenrollment date, and global data-end.
grading_logic: Must classify each patient's follow-up end as death vs disenrollment vs data-end (mutually exclusive, earliest applicable), not conflate them. Ignoring the reason observation stops, or equating disenrollment/data-end with death, is the error.
