approaches.name: three_way_terminal
approaches.description: Assigns death / disenrollment / data-end by earliest applicable, exclusive

approaches.name: conflated_end
approaches.description: Conflates the terminal reasons or ignores why follow-up ends

prompt: For each patient, identify their first qualifying diabetes diagnosis and report the count by diagnosis type; when multiple qualifying diagnoses occur on the same first date, count the patient once.
what_it_tests: Same-day tie-break for 'first' event: when a patient has multiple qualifying diagnoses on their earliest date, 'the first' is ambiguous — a naive MIN(date) join returns MULTIPLE rows for that patient, double-counting them across diagnosis types. A one-shot query joins on the minimum date without collapsing ties, inflating per-type counts and total > patient count. Correct handling applies a deterministic tie-break (or counts the patient once) so each patient contributes exactly one first event.
grading_logic: Must ensure each patient contributes exactly one first event despite same-date ties (deterministic tie-break or count-once), so per-type counts sum to the distinct patient count. A MIN(date) join that returns multiple same-day rows per patient is the error.

approaches.name: deterministic_tiebreak
approaches.description: Resolves same-day ties so each patient has one first event

approaches.name: mindate_multi
approaches.description: MIN(date) join returns multiple same-day rows, double-counting patients

prompt: Produce a transition matrix of counts of observed movements between consecutive recorded CKD stages across all patients (e.g. stage 2 to stage 3), collapsing consecutive same-stage records first. Report the matrix.
what_it_tests: Consecutive-state transition counting: a transition is a change between a patient's TEMPORALLY ADJACENT distinct states after collapsing repeats — so stage2,stage2,stage3 yields one 2->3 transition, not two. A one-shot query cross-joins all stage pairs per patient (counting non-adjacent and self pairs) or counts every record pair, inflating the matrix. Correct handling orders states, collapses runs, and tallies adjacent (from,to) pairs.
grading_logic: Must collapse consecutive same-stage records, then count only temporally adjacent (from->to) stage pairs into the matrix. Cross-joining all stage pairs or counting non-collapsed adjacent duplicates is the error.

approaches.name: adjacent_transitions
approaches.description: Collapses runs; tallies temporally adjacent from->to pairs

approaches.name: all_pairs
approaches.description: Counts all stage pairs / uncollapsed duplicates, inflating the matrix

prompt: Count patients who had an abnormal cardiac stress test that was followed by a coronary angiography within 90 days, and then a revascularization procedure. Report the count.
what_it_tests: Event-ordering dependency: the answer requires a strict temporal SEQUENCE — abnormal stress test, THEN angiography within 90 days, THEN revascularization (after the angiography). A one-shot query typically writes flat co-occurrence filters and ignores ordering, counting patients who had all three in any order. Correct handling reasons about per-patient event order and inter-event windows.
grading_logic: System must enforce the temporal order (stress test -> angiography within 90d -> later revascularization) using event dates per patient. Counting patients who have all three procedures without ordering/windowing is the error.

approaches.name: ordered_windowed
approaches.description: Enforces stress->angiography(<=90d)->revascularization order per patient

approaches.name: unordered_cooccurrence
approaches.description: Counts patients with all three procedures regardless of order/timing

prompt: Count patients whose first-ever diagnosis of chronic kidney disease occurred AFTER their first diagnosis of type 2 diabetes. Report the count.
what_it_tests: First-event ordering: the answer depends on comparing the FIRST occurrence date of two conditions per patient (CKD onset after T2D onset). A one-shot query that just requires both diagnoses present (or compares any CKD date to any T2D date) mis-answers. Correct handling computes MIN(date) per condition per patient and compares the anchors.
grading_logic: System must compute each patient's first (earliest) T2D date and first CKD date and count only those where first CKD > first T2D. Using any-date co-occurrence, or not anchoring on first occurrence, is the error.

approaches.name: first_event_ordering
approaches.description: Compares MIN(CKD date) > MIN(T2D date) per patient

approaches.name: cooccurrence_or_anydate
approaches.description: Counts patients with both diagnoses without first-occurrence ordering

prompt: Count patients whose first opioid prescription came AFTER their first documented chronic pain diagnosis (not before). Report the count.
what_it_tests: First-event ordering across two domains: requires comparing MIN(pain diagnosis date) to MIN(opioid Rx date) per patient and keeping only opioid-after-pain. A one-shot query that requires both present, or compares arbitrary dates, mis-answers.
grading_logic: Must compute first pain-diagnosis date and first opioid-Rx date per patient and count only those with first opioid > first pain. Co-occurrence or non-first-event date comparison is the error.

approaches.name: first_event_order
approaches.description: Compares MIN(opioid date) > MIN(pain dx date) per patient

approaches.name: cooccurrence
approaches.description: Counts patients with both, ignoring first-event ordering

prompt: Count patients diagnosed with lung cancer whose diagnosis was preceded by a chest CT within the prior 90 days (a workup-then-diagnosis pattern). Report the count.
what_it_tests: Directional pre-event window (ordering): the CT must come BEFORE the cancer diagnosis, within 90 days prior. A one-shot query commonly checks 'has lung cancer AND has chest CT' or uses a symmetric window, capturing post-diagnosis surveillance CTs too. Correct handling enforces CT-before-diagnosis within the prior-90-day window.
grading_logic: Must require a chest CT dated within the 90 days BEFORE the lung-cancer diagnosis, per patient (directional). Counting any CT (including after diagnosis) or ignoring the window is the error.

approaches.name: pre_window_directional
approaches.description: Requires chest CT in the 90 days before the cancer diagnosis

approaches.name: any_ct
approaches.description: Counts any lung-cancer patient with any chest CT, ignoring direction/window

prompt: Among patients newly diagnosed with heart failure, what is the median time to first hospitalization? Report the median in days.
what_it_tests: Time-to-event with right-censoring: patients who disenroll or reach data end WITHOUT being hospitalized are censored, not absent. Taking the median only over patients who were hospitalized (ignoring censored follow-up) badly underestimates the median time — and the true median may be un-reached (>50% never hospitalized). A one-shot query computes the mean/median of observed event times among those with the event. Correct handling accounts for censored follow-up (Kaplan-Meier median or explicit at-risk reasoning), or states the median is not reached.
grading_logic: Must incorporate censored follow-up (patients without the event contribute at-risk time; median from a survival/at-risk estimate, or reported as not-reached if <50% have the event). Taking the median of event times only among those hospitalized is the error.

approaches.name: censored_median
approaches.description: Uses survival/at-risk logic incl. censored patients (or reports not-reached)

approaches.name: observed_only
approaches.description: Median over hospitalized patients only, ignoring censoring

prompt: For heart failure in 2022, report the count at five levels: distinct patients, distinct hospitalization episodes, distinct encounters, distinct claims, and claim lines. Report all five.
what_it_tests: Unit-of-analysis integrity: the same clinical reality yields very different numbers at patient / episode / encounter / claim / line grain, and conflating them is a classic RWE error. The question forces the system to compute each grain correctly (distinct patients, collapsed episodes, distinct encounters, raw claims, raw lines). A one-shot query returns one COUNT(*) at whatever grain the table happens to be, unaware of the distinction.
grading_logic: Must produce five distinct counts at the patient, episode (collapsed), encounter, claim, and claim-line grains — each computed at its correct level of aggregation. A single COUNT at one grain is the error.

approaches.name: five_grains
approaches.description: Computes distinct-patient, episode, encounter, claim, and line counts separately

approaches.name: single_grain
approaches.description: Returns one COUNT(*) without distinguishing units of analysis

prompt: How many patients had a follow-up hepatitis B vaccination within one year of their first dose? Report the count under each interpretation of 'within one year': within 365 days, within 366 days on a leap year, and on or before the same calendar date next year.
what_it_tests: Competing definitions of 'within one year': '365 days', 'the same calendar date next year' (which is 366 days across a leap year), and 'by the first anniversary' are DIFFERENT boundaries yielding different counts for events near the edge. A one-shot query silently equates 'one year' with a single arithmetic (usually 365 days) and hides the divergence. Correct handling computes each interpretation and surfaces that the answer depends on the definition.
grading_logic: Must compute the count under each distinct 'within one year' interpretation (365-day, calendar-anniversary incl. leap-year effect) and surface the divergence, not silently pick one. Collapsing all senses into a single 365-day rule is the error.

approaches.name: multiple_definitions
approaches.description: Computes each 'within one year' definition and reports the divergence

approaches.name: single_arithmetic
approaches.description: Silently uses one interpretation (365 days), hiding the difference
